IronStore Product Catalog
Rugs & Carpets
Last reviewed in August 2026
Internal product reference
Market: European Union and United Kingdom
Currency: EUR (€)
Prices: Standard consumer prices including applicable VAT unless otherwise stated.
Stock status: Availability reflects the latest catalog review and may change independently of this document.
Page 1 — Catalog Scope and Operating Notes
This catalog contains products assigned to the Rugs & Carpets category in the IronStore product information
system. It includes area rugs, runners, children’s rugs, outdoor rugs, washable rugs, flatweaves, shag rugs,
natural-fibre rugs, carpet tiles, and selected premium hand-finished products.
Availability definitions
  In stock: Product is available for immediate allocation from the listed warehouse.
  Limited stock: Fewer than 15 sellable units are available across the network.
  Available to order: Product is not currently held in local inventory but can be replenished from the approved

  Available to order: Product is not currently held in local inventory but can be replenished from the approved
supplier.
  Pre-order: Product is scheduled for a future inbound shipment.
  Discontinued: Product is no longer available for new purchase. Remaining units may be retained for returns,
replacements, or clearance processing.
Warehouse codes
| Code | Location | Primary role |
|---|---|---|
| NL-RTM | Rotterdam, Netherlands | Benelux and Western Europe fulfilment |
| DE-HAM | Hamburg, Germany | Central Europe fulfilment |
| PL-WRO | Wroc■aw, Poland | Eastern Europe fulfilment |
| ES-ZAZ | Zaragoza, Spain | Iberia and Southern Europe fulfilment |
| IT-PIA | Piacenza, Italy | Premium home-textile stock |
| SE-MAL | Malmö, Sweden | Nordic fulfilment |
Product data conventions

Dimensions are shown as length × width in centimetres unless specified otherwise. Rug dimensions may vary by
approximately 2–4% for handwoven or hand-knotted products. Product weights are approximate shipping weights.
Colour descriptions are internal colour names and should not be treated as exact colour standards.

Page 46 — Product and Fulfilment Notes
Common customer-service checks
Before approving a replacement or exchange, verify:
1. SKU and dimension match the original order.
2. Product construction is compatible with the customer’s intended location.
3. The returned item has not been machine washed when the care instructions prohibit washing.
4. Any reported shedding, pile shading, edge curling, or colour variation is assessed against the product construction.
5. Outdoor products have not been stored wet or exposed to permanent weather conditions.
6. Carpet-tile orders are checked by tile count rather than area-rug unit count.
Standard dimensional guidance

6. Carpet-tile orders are checked by tile count rather than area-rug unit count.
Standard dimensional guidance
  Small rugs: Typically below 120 × 180 cm.
  Medium rugs: Approximately 140 × 200 cm to 180 × 270 cm.
  Large rugs: Approximately 200 × 300 cm and above.
  Runners: Narrow rectangular products generally between 60 and 90 cm wide.
  Round rugs: Diameter is used as the primary dimension.
  Carpet tiles: Sold individually unless the product listing explicitly specifies a carton quantity.
Underlay guidance

Underlay is recommended for most loose rugs on laminate, tile, polished wood, vinyl, and other smooth floors.
Underlay improves stability and can reduce wear caused by repeated movement. For hand-knotted, handwoven,
high-pile, and natural-fibre rugs, a breathable underlay is preferred.
Returns and storage
Rugs must be stored dry and protected from direct sunlight. Rolled products should remain on a suitable core where
possible. Folded storage can result in permanent crease lines, especially in latex-backed or high-pile products.
Natural-fibre rugs must not be stored in unventilated plastic wrapping.

Size and fit conventions
IronStore uses EU sizing for most apparel. Where a supplier uses inch-based measurements, the product record
includes waist and inseam values. Fit descriptions are standardized as follows:
  Slim fit: Close to the body with limited ease
  Regular fit: Standard ease through chest, waist, or hip
  Relaxed fit: Additional ease for comfort and layering
  Oversized fit: Deliberately broader proportions and longer or dropped construction
  Compression fit: Close-fitting technical garment intended to provide support
Customers should be directed to the product-specific size chart when available. Size charts are maintained
separately from this catalog and may vary between product families.

assorted and themed products.

Data Privacy & GDPR Compliance Policy
Owning area: Legal_Terms
Policy ID: LEG-PRV-001
Version: 4.2
Last reviewed: August 2026
Policy owner: Group Data Protection Officer (DPO)
1. Purpose and Overview
This policy defines how IronStore collects, uses, stores, shares, and protects personal data in accordance with the
General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), applicable national privacy laws, and contractual obligations.
IronStore sells consumer products across Europe, including electronics, home essentials, clothing, outdoor
equipment, beauty products, and related categories. The policy applies to customer, employee, supplier, courier,
marketplace, and website visitor data processed through IronStore systems or on its behalf.
Compliance is mandatory. Business teams must involve Legal_Terms before launching processing activities that
create new privacy risks, introduce new tracking technologies, or materially change how personal data is used.
2. Scope
This policy applies to:

create new privacy risks, introduce new tracking technologies, or materially change how personal data is used.
2. Scope
This policy applies to:
  IronStore GmbH and all European subsidiaries and branches.
  Employees, temporary workers, contractors, and approved service providers.
  Customer-facing websites, mobile applications, marketplaces, customer service channels, and fulfilment
operations.
  Personal data in production, test, support, analytics, backup, and paper environments.
  Processing performed by third parties under an IronStore contract.
The policy covers personal data relating to identified or identifiable individuals. Anonymous information, which cannot
reasonably be linked to an individual, is outside the GDPR but must still be handled securely.
3. Policy Statement and Procedures
3.1 Core Privacy Principles
IronStore processes personal data according to these principles:
  Lawfulness, fairness, and transparency: use a valid legal basis and provide clear notices.

  Lawfulness, fairness, and transparency: use a valid legal basis and provide clear notices.
  Purpose limitation: use data only for defined, compatible business purposes.

  Data minimisation: collect only information necessary for the stated purpose.
  Accuracy: enable correction and remove data that is no longer reliable.
  Storage limitation: retain data only for approved periods.
  Integrity and confidentiality: protect data against unauthorised access, loss, alteration, or disclosure.
  Accountability: maintain evidence of decisions, controls, training, and reviews.
No team may use customer data for a new purpose merely because the data is already available in Salesforce,
Snowflake, Magento, or another approved system.
3.2 Lawful Basis and Transparency
The responsible business owner must document the lawful basis before processing begins. Approved bases include:
  Contract: order fulfilment, payment processing, delivery, returns, and customer account administration.
  Legal obligation: tax, accounting, product safety, fraud prevention, and regulatory reporting.

  Legal obligation: tax, accounting, product safety, fraud prevention, and regulatory reporting.
  Legitimate interests: service security, limited operational analytics, debt recovery, and carefully assessed
business communications.
  Consent: optional marketing, non-essential cookies, personalised advertising, and certain profiling activities.
  Vital interests or public task: only where specifically validated by Legal_Terms.
Marketing consent must be recorded in the ConsentHub service, including timestamp, wording presented, channel,
country, and withdrawal status. Pre-ticked boxes, bundled consent, and consent obtained through misleading wording
are prohibited.
Every customer-facing collection point must link to the current Privacy Notice. Material changes require approval
from Legal_Terms and, where appropriate, renewed consent.
3.3 Data Collection and Classification
Teams must classify information in the IronStore Data Register:

3.3 Data Collection and Classification
Teams must classify information in the IronStore Data Register:
  Public: information approved for public release.
  Internal: routine business information with limited impact if disclosed.
  Confidential: personal data, commercial information, and customer records.
  Restricted: payment data, identity documents, authentication secrets, health information, or high-risk
combinations of data.
Sensitive or special-category data must not be collected unless expressly required, legally justified, and approved by
the DPO. Payment card numbers must not be stored in IronStore applications; payments must use the tokenised
Adyen platform.
Production personal data must not be copied into development or training environments. Where testing requires
realistic records, teams must use synthetic data or an approved anonymisation process.
3.4 Access Control and Security

System owners must apply least-privilege access and review permissions at least quarterly. Access to restricted data
requires multi-factor authentication through Microsoft Entra ID and must be logged.
Minimum controls include:
  Role-based access in Magento Commerce, Salesforce Service Cloud, Snowflake, and warehouse systems.
  Encryption in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and encryption at rest for hosted databases.
  Endpoint protection and managed device controls through Microsoft Intune.
  Central security monitoring in Microsoft Sentinel.
  Immediate access removal when employment or supplier access ends.
  No transmission of customer files through personal email, consumer file-sharing services, or unapproved
messaging applications.
Exporting more than 10,000 customer records, or any restricted dataset, requires written approval from the system
owner and the DPO or delegated Privacy Counsel.
3.5 Retention and Deletion

owner and the DPO or delegated Privacy Counsel.
3.5 Retention and Deletion
The approved retention schedule is maintained in LEG-PRV-004 Data Retention Standard. Unless a longer period
is required by law, contract, or an active dispute:
  Order, invoice, and tax records: 10 years after the relevant financial year.
  Customer account data: until account closure, then deleted or anonymised within 90 days.
  Customer service cases: 3 years after closure.
  Marketing suppression records: retained only to honour opt-out requests.
  Delivery and returns records: 3 years after completion.
  Web analytics identifiers: 14 months, unless a shorter consent setting applies.
  CCTV footage at fulfilment sites: normally 30 days, subject to incident preservation.
Deletion jobs run monthly through the Data Lifecycle Manager. Legal holds, fraud investigations, chargebacks, and
regulatory requests suspend deletion for the affected records. Business owners must document the reason and

regulatory requests suspend deletion for the affected records. Business owners must document the reason and
expected end date.
3.6 Individual Rights Requests
Individuals may exercise rights through the privacy form on IronStore.eu, by emailing privacy@ironstore.eu, or
through Customer Support. Requests must be recorded in PrivacyDesk and acknowledged within five business
days.
The Privacy Operations team must:
1. Verify identity using proportionate checks; do not request unnecessary identity documents.
2. Search relevant systems, including CRM, order, marketing, support, and consent records.
3. Consult Legal_Terms where exemptions, third-party data, or complex searches apply.

4. Respond without undue delay and normally within one month.
5. Extend the deadline by up to two additional months only where the request is complex; notify the requester within
the first month.
6. Record the outcome, search scope, approvals, and response date.
Requests include access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability, objection, and withdrawal of consent. Automated
decisions with legal or similarly significant effects require a documented human review route.
3.7 Cookies, Tracking, and Profiling
Non-essential cookies, advertising pixels, session replay, and similar technologies require prior consent in the
CookieHub CMP. Strictly necessary technologies may operate without consent where legally permitted.
The Web Product team must:
  Maintain an approved tag inventory.
  Block unconsented tags before consent is recorded.
  Re-scan production websites monthly.
  Obtain Privacy Engineering approval before adding a new vendor tag.

  Re-scan production websites monthly.
  Obtain Privacy Engineering approval before adding a new vendor tag.
  Record vendor, purpose, data categories, retention, and transfer location.
Personalised recommendations may use purchase and browsing data only for documented purposes. High-impact
profiling, sensitive inferences, or combined datasets require a DPIA and DPO approval before deployment.
3.8 Suppliers and International Transfers
Procurement must involve Legal_Terms before a supplier receives personal data. Contracts must include appropriate
data processing terms, confidentiality, security controls, subprocessor notification, audit rights, deletion or return
obligations, and assistance with GDPR rights.
The supplier must be listed in the Vendor Privacy Register. Data Processing Agreements are mandatory for
processors unless Legal_Terms documents a justified exception.
Transfers outside the European Economic Area require an approved mechanism, such as:
  An adequacy decision.

Transfers outside the European Economic Area require an approved mechanism, such as:
  An adequacy decision.
  EU Standard Contractual Clauses.
  Binding Corporate Rules.
  A documented derogation for an occasional, necessary transfer.
Legal_Terms must complete a Transfer Impact Assessment where required. Teams may not approve a vendor’s
standard international transfer terms without review.
3.9 Data Protection Impact Assessments
A DPIA is required before processing likely to create a high risk to individuals, including:

  Large-scale profiling or behavioural advertising.
  Systematic monitoring of public areas or workers.
  Processing special-category data at scale.
  Biometric identification or significant automated decision-making.
  Combining datasets from multiple business functions.
  A new technology that materially changes the risk profile.
The project owner completes the DPIA Template LEG-PRV-006 with Security and Engineering. The DPO approves,
rejects, or requires mitigations before go-live. Unresolved high risks must be referred to the relevant supervisory
authority where legally required.
3.10 Incidents and Personal Data Breaches
Employees must report suspected loss, unauthorised access, misdirected emails, ransomware, or accidental
disclosure immediately through security@ironstore.eu and the ServiceNow Security Incident form. Reports
should be made within one hour where possible.

should be made within one hour where possible.
Security Operations leads containment and evidence preservation. The DPO assesses notification requirements with
Legal_Terms:
  Supervisory authority notification is targeted within 72 hours of becoming aware of a reportable breach.
  Affected individuals are notified without undue delay where the risk is high.
  All incidents, including non-reportable events, are recorded in the Breach Register.
  Employees must not contact regulators, customers, or media about an incident unless authorised.
3.11 Training and Monitoring
All personnel complete privacy and information security training during onboarding and annually thereafter. Customer
Support, Marketing, Product, Engineering, HR, and fulfilment managers receive role-specific training.
Compliance is monitored through quarterly access reviews, annual supplier assessments, retention-job reports,

Compliance is monitored through quarterly access reviews, annual supplier assessments, retention-job reports,
cookie scans, and internal audits. Repeated non-compliance may result in access restrictions, disciplinary action,
contract termination, or escalation to the Executive Risk Committee.
4. Roles and Responsibilities

  Legal_Terms / Privacy Counsel: approves notices, contracts, lawful-basis assessments, DPIAs, transfers, and

Policy Statement / Procedures

Each territory-specific version must identify, where applicable:

  Registered office and customer service contact details.

  Local withdrawal, warranty, and complaint rights.
  Accepted payment methods and delivery limitations.

drafting only and must not be published without human review.

2. Customer Account and Acceptable Use
Customers may create an account using accurate information and must keep login credentials confidential. One
person must not create accounts for abusive, fraudulent, or automated purchasing activity.
IronStore may suspend or restrict an account where there is credible evidence of:
  Payment fraud, chargeback abuse, or identity misuse.
  Bot activity, bulk purchasing, or voucher exploitation.
  Harassment of employees, sellers, or delivery partners.
  Attempts to interfere with site security or service availability.
  Repeated misuse of return, refund, or replacement processes.
Account restrictions must be recorded in CaseHub with the reason code, evidence link, decision owner, and review
date. Permanent closure or restriction of access to statutory rights requires Legal approval.
Customers must not:
  Use scraping, automated checkout, or unauthorised browser extensions.

Customers must not:
  Use scraping, automated checkout, or unauthorised browser extensions.
  Upload malware, unlawful content, or another person’s personal data.
  Resell IronStore promotional benefits where prohibited by promotion rules.

Customer-facing suspension messages must be factual, proportionate, and limited to the information necessary to
protect IronStore’s legitimate interests.

  Delivery costs, estimated delivery timeframe, and delivery restrictions.

  Seller identity for marketplace products.
  Availability status and any purchase quantity limits.

4. Order Acceptance and Payment
An order confirmation acknowledges receipt of the customer’s order. It does not necessarily mean that IronStore has

The checkout flow must:
  Display the selected products, quantities, total price, delivery charges, and applicable taxes.

The checkout flow must:

Payments are processed through approved providers connected to Adyen and Checkout.com. Teams must not

5. Delivery, Cancellation, and Returns
The delivery promise shown at checkout must be based on the fulfilment service level recorded in OMS Atlas. If a
delivery is delayed, Customer Operations must provide the customer with an updated estimate and the available legal

Customers may have a statutory right to withdraw from distance contracts. The relevant period, exclusions, return
method, and refund process must be stated in the country version of the Terms.
Returns processing requirements:
  Return requests are logged in ReturnFlow against the order number.
  Eligibility is assessed using the applicable territory rules.
  Refund decisions are based on receipt, product condition, and statutory rights.
  Refunds must not be withheld solely because a customer used a preferred return carrier where the Terms
permit another method.

permit another method.

Customer Operations should acknowledge a return or complaint within two business days. Standard refund
processing is five business days after the return is approved, subject to payment-provider timelines.
6. Product Defects, Warranties, and Complaints
IronStore must distinguish between:
  Statutory consumer remedies.
  Voluntary manufacturer or IronStore warranties.
  Commercial goodwill offers.
  Marketplace seller obligations.
Agents must not describe a goodwill replacement as a waiver of statutory rights. Defect claims must be recorded in
CaseHub with photographs, product identifiers, purchase date, and the remedy offered.
Safety complaints, suspected counterfeit products, and repeated product failures must be escalated within one

Safety complaints, suspected counterfeit products, and repeated product failures must be escalated within one
business day to Product Compliance and the Legal Duty Manager. A product may be temporarily delisted where risk
is credible and cannot be mitigated immediately.
Formal legal complaints, regulator correspondence, and pre-action letters must be forwarded to Legal Operations on

implementation must be tested in staging, including expired, combined, refunded, and partially used vouchers.
Reviews must reflect genuine customer experiences. Moderation may remove content that is unlawful, defamatory,
discriminatory, irrelevant, fraudulent, or contains personal data. Negative reviews must not be removed merely

1. Purpose and Overview
This workflow defines how IronStore contracts must be requested, reviewed, approved, signed, stored, and
monitored. It is intended to ensure that contracts are commercially sound, legally compliant, accurately recorded, and
approved by the appropriate budget and risk owners.
The workflow applies to supplier, logistics, technology, marketing, employment-related commercial, marketplace,
consulting, real estate, and other business agreements. No employee may commit IronStore to contractual
obligations outside this process.
Contracts must be handled through the designated systems and approval chains. Email approval alone is not
sufficient unless specifically permitted under this document.

sufficient unless specifically permitted under this document.
2. Scope
This workflow applies to:
  New contracts, statements of work, order forms, amendments, renewals, and termination agreements.
  Contracts with suppliers, service providers, brands, agencies, landlords, technology vendors, and business
partners.
  Agreements involving IronStore entities in the EU, EEA, United Kingdom, or Switzerland.
  Contracts that process personal data, create intellectual property obligations, or involve customer-facing
services.
  Purchases and commitments with a total expected value of €5,000 or more, including committed renewal
periods.
The workflow does not replace specialist review required for:
  Employment contracts and employee relations matters.
  Product safety, customs, tax, or regulated product assessments.
  Information security assessments for technology or data-processing services.
  Real estate transactions or material financing arrangements.

Low-value purchases made through an approved catalogue or standard procurement channel may follow the

3. Policy Statement
All contracts must:

  Identify the correct IronStore contracting entity and authorised signatory.
  State pricing, currency, taxes, invoicing terms, service scope, and contract duration clearly.
  Include appropriate confidentiality, data protection, intellectual property, liability, termination, and governing-law
provisions.
  Be stored in IronStore ContractHub before signature or, for urgent exceptions, within five business days after
signature.
  Be approved before any purchase order, service commencement, public announcement, or supplier
onboarding.
Employees must not:

4. Contract Approval Procedure
4.1 Initiate the request
The business owner creates a contract request in Coupa and links it to the relevant purchase requisition, budget line,
or project code.
The request must include:

  Contract type and short description of the service or goods.
  Estimated total value, including extensions, minimum commitments, and implementation fees.
  Proposed start date, end date, renewal mechanism, and notice period.

The requestor is responsible for providing complete and accurate information. Incomplete requests may be returned
without review.
4.2 Select the contract route
The requestor selects one of the following routes:
Standard route
Used for approved IronStore templates with no material changes and a value below €100,000. Procurement and the
budget owner complete the commercial approval. Legal review is required for any deviation from the template.
Legal review route
Required where the counterparty uses its own terms, the contract contains non-standard risk, or the value is
€100,000 or more. Legal reviews the agreement in ContractHub and records comments, issues, and approval
status.
Enhanced review route
Required for:
  Personal-data processing or customer-data access.

status.

1. Purpose and Overview
This playbook defines the standard sales approach for IronStore’s consumer-product business. It provides a common
operating model for acquiring, qualifying, converting, and retaining customers across electronics, home essentials,
clothing, outdoor equipment, beauty, and related categories.
IronStore primarily serves consumers through its online storefronts and mobile channels. Sales activity must support
profitable growth, accurate customer communication, compliant data handling, and a consistent customer experience
across markets.
The playbook applies to direct sales activity, marketplace opportunities, affiliate partnerships, business-to-business

across markets.
The playbook applies to direct sales activity, marketplace opportunities, affiliate partnerships, business-to-business
enquiries, and promotional campaigns managed by Sales or in partnership with Marketing, Merchandising, and
Customer Operations.
2. Scope
This document covers:
  Customer and opportunity qualification.
  Sales pipeline management in Salesforce.
  Pricing, promotions, discounts, and commercial approvals.
  Sales handover to Customer Operations, Finance, and Fulfilment.
  Key account and partner management.
  Performance reporting and required sales hygiene.
  Escalation of legal, financial, reputational, or customer-risk issues.
This playbook does not replace:
  Country-specific consumer protection or VAT requirements.

3. Sales Operating Principles
IronStore sales activity is governed by the following principles:
  Customer clarity: Prices, delivery estimates, stock status, warranties, and return conditions must be accurate
and understandable.
  Profitable growth: Revenue targets do not justify selling below approved margin, concealing fees, or making
unsupported claims.
  One source of truth: Salesforce is the official record for managed opportunities, partner discussions, forecasts,
and commercial approvals.
  Evidence-based decisions: Forecasts and proposals must use current pricing, stock, demand, and margin
data.
  Compliant communication: Outreach must follow consent, opt-out, and country-specific direct-marketing
rules.
  Fast ownership: Every active opportunity must have a named owner, next action, and due date.

Purpose and Overview
This plan defines how IronStore sales employees earn variable commission for profitable, compliant revenue
generation. It applies to sales activity across IronStore’s European e-commerce operations, including consumer
electronics, home essentials, clothing, outdoor equipment, beauty products, and other approved categories.
The plan is designed to reward sustainable sales rather than order volume alone. Commission is based on eligible
net revenue, contribution margin, customer quality, and achievement against approved targets. Payments are subject
to order validation, returns processing, fraud controls, and payroll requirements.
The plan is reviewed annually by Sales Operations, Finance, People, and Legal. The Director of Sales must approve
any exception before it is communicated to an employee.

any exception before it is communicated to an employee.
Scope
This plan applies to:
  Account Executives, Sales Specialists, and approved Marketplace Sales Managers.
  Employees assigned an individual or team sales target in Workday.
  Permanent employees and fixed-term employees whose contracts expressly include variable pay.
  Sales generated in approved European markets and recorded in the assigned Salesforce opportunity or channel
account.
This plan does not apply to:
  Customer Service, warehouse, procurement, or affiliate employees unless separately covered by a written
incentive plan.
  Contractors, agency workers, interns, or employees on plans that expressly replace this plan.
  Orders generated solely through paid media, automated campaigns, or customer self-service without
documented sales ownership.
  Revenue from prohibited products, internal purchases, test orders, fraudulent transactions, or policy violations.
Policy Statement

Commission is earned only when an eligible order meets all validation requirements. A booked order is not
automatically commissionable. Revenue must be attributable to the employee, accepted by the customer, and not
excluded under this plan.
IronStore may correct, defer, reduce, or recover commission where an order is returned, cancelled, refunded, unpaid,
incorrectly attributed, or found to breach commercial or compliance rules. Changes are applied in the next practical
payroll cycle and are documented in the Commission Management Portal.
No employee may offer unapproved discounts, alter customer ownership, split orders, or delay cancellations to
influence commission. Suspected manipulation is handled under the Sales Conduct Standard and may result in
disciplinary action.
Commission Structure
Target and On-Target Earnings
Each eligible employee receives the following information in Workday before the start of the plan year:
  Annual sales target.
  Target commission amount.

  Annual sales target.
  Target commission amount.
  Commission period and currency.
  Individual or team weighting.
  Applicable product-category modifiers.
  Threshold, accelerator, and maximum rules.
The standard plan year runs from 1 January to 31 December. Employees joining or leaving during the year receive a
prorated target based on active employment days, subject to their employment contract and local law.
Unless otherwise stated:
  70% of commission is based on individual eligible net revenue.
  30% is based on the assigned team target.
  Employees with no individual portfolio use a 100% team-based measure.
  Targets are adjusted only for approved transfers, extended leave, territory changes, or material business
restructuring.
Eligible Net Revenue
Eligible net revenue is calculated as:
Customer invoice value excluding VAT, delivery charges, gift cards, refunds, cancellations, credits, and
non-commissionable fees.

Customer invoice value excluding VAT, delivery charges, gift cards, refunds, cancellations, credits, and
non-commissionable fees.
Revenue is credited to the employee who is recorded as the primary owner in Salesforce at the time the order is
accepted in the Order Management System (OMS). Split credit requires approval from the Sales Manager and Sales
Operations before month-end close.

The following are excluded:
  Orders below the approved minimum margin.
  Employee, test, or related-party purchases.
  Orders later identified as fraudulent or sanctioned-party transactions.
  Free replacements, warranty fulfilment, and goodwill orders.
  Revenue generated by an unapproved reseller or marketplace channel.
  Orders where the employee did not perform a documented sales activity.
Margin and Category Modifiers
Commission is calculated using the standard category rate table maintained by Finance. The current default rates
are:
  Standard categories: 1.0% of eligible net revenue.
  Strategic or high-margin categories: 1.25%.
  Low-margin or clearance categories: 0.50%.
  Approved new-market launches: 1.50% for the first 90 days, subject to Finance approval.
A category modifier applies based on the product classification in the Product Information Management system (PIM),

Quota Attainment
The standard attainment curve is:

Accelerators apply only after the relevant threshold is reached and do not retroactively increase commission on

customer trust, and compliance with applicable European consumer and advertising requirements. No promotion may

The standard promotion record is the source of truth. It must be maintained in PromoHub, with links to the campaign

1. Purpose and Overview
This policy defines the minimum security requirements for IronStore’s information systems, devices, applications, and
data. IronStore operates across Europe and processes customer, employee, supplier, payment, and operational
information. Security controls must protect confidentiality, integrity, availability, and legal compliance.
The policy supports IronStore’s obligations under applicable European data protection and cybersecurity
requirements, including the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the NIS2 Directive where applicable, and
local employment and regulatory requirements. It applies a risk-based approach: higher-risk systems and data
require stronger controls, closer monitoring, and more frequent review.

require stronger controls, closer monitoring, and more frequent review.
All employees, contractors, temporary workers, and third parties with access to IronStore resources must comply with
this policy. Failure to comply may result in access removal, disciplinary action, contract termination, or legal action.
2. Scope
This policy applies to:
  IronStore corporate offices, warehouses, fulfilment sites, and remote working environments.
  Company-managed laptops, mobile devices, servers, network equipment, and storage.
  Cloud services, including Microsoft 365, Azure, Shopify Plus, Salesforce, Jira, and Snowflake.
  Customer, employee, supplier, financial, payment, product, and operational data.
  Employees, contractors, agency workers, service providers, and approved business partners.
  Systems developed, operated, or procured by IronStore, including mobile applications and e-commerce
platforms.

  Systems developed, operated, or procured by IronStore, including mobile applications and e-commerce
platforms.
Personal devices may access IronStore systems only through an approved Bring Your Own Device (BYOD)
arrangement and must meet the requirements in the Device Standard.
3. Policy Statement and Procedures
3.1 Information Classification

Information owners must classify data when it is created or received. The following classifications apply:
  Public: Approved for unrestricted external release, such as published product descriptions.
  Internal: Routine business information intended for IronStore personnel.
  Confidential: Information that could cause material harm if disclosed, including contracts, pricing plans, source
code, and supplier terms.
  Restricted: Highly sensitive information requiring enhanced controls, including payment-related data, identity
documents, authentication secrets, health information, and unmasked customer records.
Requirements:
  Restricted data must be encrypted in transit and at rest.
  Confidential and Restricted data must not be sent to personal email, consumer file-sharing services, or
unapproved AI or productivity tools.
  Access must be granted on a least-privilege and need-to-know basis.
  Data owners must review access to Restricted repositories at least quarterly.

  Data owners must review access to Restricted repositories at least quarterly.
  Suspected loss or unauthorised disclosure must be reported to the Security Operations mailbox immediately.
3.2 Identity and Access Management
IronStore uses Microsoft Entra ID as the primary identity provider and requires centralised authentication wherever
technically possible.
  Each individual must use a unique IronStore account. Shared accounts are prohibited unless approved by
Information Security.
  Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for Microsoft 365, VPN, cloud consoles, administrative tools, and
production systems.
  Phishing-resistant MFA, such as FIDO2 security keys or passkeys, is required for privileged administrators and
payment-platform administrators.
  Access requests must be approved by the user’s line manager and the relevant system owner.
  Privileged access requires an additional approval from the IT Security Manager.

  Privileged access requires an additional approval from the IT Security Manager.
  Access must be removed within four hours of a confirmed termination and by the end of the worker’s last day for
planned departures.
  Role changes must trigger an access review within five business days.
  Dormant accounts are disabled after 45 days unless the system owner documents a business reason.
  Passwords must be unique, stored only in the approved password manager, and never shared through chat or
email.
  Service accounts must have a named owner, documented purpose, restricted permissions, and secrets rotated
at least every 180 days.
Quarterly, system owners must certify access to critical systems, including the order management platform,
warehouse management system, ERP, customer service platform, and payment administration consoles.
3.3 Endpoint and Mobile Security

All company-managed endpoints must be enrolled in Microsoft Intune and protected by Microsoft Defender for
Endpoint.
Minimum requirements include:
  Automatic operating system and application updates.
  Full-disk encryption using BitLocker or an approved equivalent.
  Screen lock after a maximum of 10 minutes of inactivity.
  Endpoint detection and response enabled and reporting to the Security Operations Centre (SOC).
  Local administrator rights removed unless a documented exception is approved.
  Approved endpoint firewall and anti-malware controls enabled.
  Corporate data stored only in approved locations, such as OneDrive, SharePoint, or managed application
storage.
Lost or stolen devices must be reported to the Service Desk within one hour of discovery. IT may remotely lock or
wipe the device. Employees must not disable security software, install unapproved software, or connect unknown
USB devices to company equipment.

wipe the device. Employees must not disable security software, install unapproved software, or connect unknown
USB devices to company equipment.
Remote work must use a private, access-controlled network. Public Wi-Fi may be used only with the IronStore VPN
or an approved zero-trust connection. Confidential discussions must not take place where unauthorised people can
overhear them.
3.4 Network, Cloud, and Application Security
The Infrastructure team must maintain separate development, test, and production environments. Production access
must be restricted, logged, and reviewed.
  Internet-facing services must be protected by approved web application firewall and distributed denial-of-service
controls.
  Administrative interfaces must not be directly exposed to the public internet.
  Network security groups and firewall rules require documented owners and annual review.
  Critical cloud services must use central logging, MFA, encryption, and region-appropriate data residency

  Critical cloud services must use central logging, MFA, encryption, and region-appropriate data residency
settings.
  Production secrets must be stored in Azure Key Vault or another approved secrets-management service.
  Customer payment data must be processed through approved payment service providers. IronStore systems
must not store full card numbers or CVV data.
  Source code must be stored in IronStore GitHub Enterprise repositories with branch protection and mandatory
peer review.
  High-risk code changes require security review before production deployment.
  Vulnerability scanning must run at least weekly for internet-facing assets and before major releases.
Development teams must use synthetic or masked data in non-production environments. Production data may be
copied to test systems only with written approval from the system owner, Data Protection Officer, and Security
Architecture lead.

3.5 Vulnerability and Patch Management
IT Security maintains the central asset and vulnerability register. Asset owners are responsible for remediation within
these limits:
  Critical vulnerabilities with known exploitation: mitigation within 24 hours and remediation within seven days.
  Other Critical vulnerabilities: remediation within 14 days.
  High vulnerabilities: remediation within 30 days.
  Medium vulnerabilities: remediation within 90 days.
  Low vulnerabilities: address during normal maintenance planning.
Where remediation is not possible, the owner must document compensating controls, business impact, and a target
date. Exceptions require approval from the Director of Information Security and expire after 90 days unless renewed.
Unsupported operating systems, applications, and network devices must not be used in production unless an
approved exception and replacement plan exist.
3.6 Logging, Monitoring, and Security Events

approved exception and replacement plan exist.
3.6 Logging, Monitoring, and Security Events
Security-relevant events must be recorded centrally in Microsoft Sentinel or an approved equivalent. Critical systems
must log authentication, privilege changes, configuration changes, administrative actions, and data export events.
  Logs must use synchronised time sources.
  Security logs must be retained for at least 12 months, subject to legal and privacy requirements.
  Restricted-data access logs must be protected from alteration.
  The SOC monitors alerts during business hours and maintains an on-call escalation rota for critical events.
  High-severity alerts must be triaged within 30 minutes.
  Log access is limited to authorised IT Security personnel and approved investigators.
Employees must report suspected phishing, malware, unauthorised access, data loss, or unusual system behaviour

Employees must report suspected phishing, malware, unauthorised access, data loss, or unusual system behaviour
through the Service Desk portal, the “Report Phishing” button, or the 24-hour security contact number listed on the
intranet. They must not investigate beyond basic safe actions or delete evidence.
3.7 Incident Response
The Incident Response Plan defines the response process. All suspected incidents are recorded in ServiceNow with
a severity, owner, timeline, and affected assets.
Response stages are:
1. Identify and contain: Confirm the event, isolate affected accounts or devices, and preserve evidence.
2. Assess: Determine affected systems, data, jurisdictions, and business impact.
3. Eradicate and recover: Remove the cause, restore services, and validate system security.

4. Notify and review: Inform management, Legal, Privacy, insurers, regulators, customers, or law enforcement
where required.
Potential personal data breaches must be reported to the Data Protection Officer immediately and no later than two
hours after discovery. The DPO determines whether regulatory notification is required. Employees must not contact
regulators, customers, or media about a security incident unless authorised.
A post-incident review must be completed within ten business days for High and Critical incidents. Actions are tracked
to closure by the Security Governance team.
3.8 Backup, Continuity, and Recovery
Critical business services, including checkout, order management, fulfilment, customer service, ERP, and identity
services, must have documented recovery requirements.
  Critical production data must be backed up daily, with more frequent replication where defined by the service
owner.

  Critical production data must be backed up daily, with more frequent replication where defined by the service
owner.
  Backups must be encrypted, access-controlled, and protected against deletion or ransomware.
  At least one backup copy must be logically or physically separated from the production environment.
  Restore tests must be completed quarterly for Tier 1 systems and annually for other critical systems.
  Recovery results and unresolved gaps must be reported to the IT Risk Committee.
Business owners must maintain manual workarounds for essential fulfilment, customer support, and payment
reconciliation activities.
3.9 Third-Party Security
Procurement and the system owner must complete a security and privacy assessment before a supplier receives
Confidential or Restricted data or connects to IronStore systems.
Contracts must address:
  Security controls and incident notification.
  Data processing responsibilities and sub-processors.

Contracts must address:
  Security controls and incident notification.
  Data processing responsibilities and sub-processors.
  Access limitation and authentication.
  Data location, retention, deletion, and return.
  Audit rights or equivalent assurance reports.
  Exit arrangements and secure transfer of data.
Critical suppliers are reviewed annually. Supplier access must be time-limited, individually assigned, MFA-protected,
and removed when the engagement ends.
3.10 Security Awareness
All personnel must complete security and privacy training within 30 days of joining IronStore and annually thereafter.
Additional training is required for developers, privileged administrators, warehouse technology users, customer

service teams, and personnel handling Restricted data.
IronStore may conduct simulated phishing exercises. Personnel who fail a simulation may be assigned targeted
training. Repeated unsafe behaviour is escalated to the individual’s manager.

Password & Access Management Policy
Policy ID: IT-SEC-04
Owning area: IT
Policy owner: Head of Infrastructure & Security
Version: 4.0
Last reviewed: August 2026
Applies to: IronStore GmbH and all European subsidiaries
Purpose / Overview
This policy defines how IronStore creates, manages, reviews, and removes access to company systems and
information. Its purpose is to reduce the risk of account compromise, unauthorised access, data loss, and operational
disruption.
Access must be based on business need, limited to the minimum required level, and removed promptly when no
longer required. IronStore uses central identity management, multi-factor authentication (MFA), role-based access
controls, and periodic access reviews to support this policy.
Scope
This policy applies to:
  Employees, temporary staff, contractors, consultants, interns, and agency workers.
  Corporate accounts, privileged accounts, service accounts, and shared technical accounts.

  Corporate accounts, privileged accounts, service accounts, and shared technical accounts.
  Company-managed laptops, mobile devices, virtual desktops, and approved personal devices used for work.
  Systems operated by IronStore or on its behalf, including:
  Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365.
  Workday, SAP S/4HANA, and finance applications.
  Shopify Plus, warehouse management systems, and logistics platforms.
  AWS, Azure, GitHub Enterprise, Jira, Confluence, and Salesforce.
  Customer support, marketing, payment, and analytics platforms.
  Third-party access to IronStore systems or data.
This policy does not replace system-specific security requirements. Where requirements conflict, the stricter
requirement applies unless the CISO approves an exception.
Policy Statement and Procedures
1. Account and Identity Standards

Each person must use an individual IronStore account. Accounts must not be shared, transferred, or used by another
person.
  Usernames follow the format firstname.lastname@ironstore.eu.
  HR must create or update the employee record before IT provisions access.
  Identity records must include the person’s legal name, manager, department, employment status, and location.
  Accounts must be linked to a unique employee or contractor identifier.
  Personal email addresses must not be used for company accounts.
  Local administrator rights are prohibited unless approved under the Privileged Access Standard.
  Dormant accounts are disabled after 30 days without successful authentication.
  Disabled accounts are deleted or archived after 90 days, subject to legal hold and retention requirements.
IT Service Desk may create a temporary account only where the request includes a named owner, business reason,
expiry date, and approving manager.
2. Password Requirements

expiry date, and approving manager.
2. Password Requirements
Passwords must be resistant to guessing and must not be reused across company and personal services.
For systems that support modern authentication:
  Passwords must be at least 14 characters long.
  Passphrases of four or more unrelated words are recommended.
  Passwords must not contain the user’s name, username, company name, product names, or common seasonal
terms.
  Passwords must not appear in the 10,000 most commonly used passwords or known breach lists.
  Password managers approved by IT, currently 1Password Business, must be used for storing corporate
credentials.
  Passwords must not be stored in browsers, spreadsheets, tickets, chat messages, or unencrypted files.
  Passwords must not be sent by email or communicated verbally.
Routine password changes are not required for standard accounts when MFA and risk-based controls are enabled. A
password must be changed immediately if:

password must be changed immediately if:
  The account may have been compromised.
  The password was disclosed, reused, or entered into an unapproved site.
  Security Operations instructs the user to change it.
  The system does not support MFA or is identified as high risk.
Systems that cannot support MFA must enforce a minimum 16-character password and a maximum password age of
180 days. Exceptions require written approval from the CISO.
3. Multi-Factor Authentication

MFA is mandatory for all externally accessible company systems and all administrative access.
  The preferred method is a FIDO2 security key or passkey.
  Authenticator applications using number matching are permitted.
  SMS may be used only as a temporary recovery method or where no stronger method is supported.
  Email-based one-time codes are not an approved primary MFA method.
  At least two MFA methods must be registered for employees with privileged or business-critical access.
  Recovery codes must be stored in the approved password manager or a secured physical location.
  Users must never approve an unexpected MFA prompt.
  Repeated unexpected prompts must be reported to the Service Desk or Security Operations immediately.
MFA resets require identity verification through the Service Desk. For privileged users, the reset must be approved by
the user’s manager or the on-call Security Operations lead.
4. Access Requests and Approval

the user’s manager or the on-call Security Operations lead.
4. Access Requests and Approval
Access is granted through the IronStore ServiceNow request catalogue. Requests must specify:
  The system, role, and access level requested.
  Business purpose and expected duration.
  The user’s manager and cost centre.
  Any customer, payment, production, or personal-data access involved.
Standard access is approved by the line manager and the system owner. Sensitive or privileged access additionally
requires approval from the relevant data owner. Production access, payment-system access, and access to customer
exports require approval from both the system owner and the Head of Infrastructure & Security.
IT fulfils approved requests through Microsoft Entra ID groups, application roles, or the CyberArk Privilege Cloud
platform. Direct permissions should not be assigned unless the system cannot support group-based access.
Target fulfilment times are:

platform. Direct permissions should not be assigned unless the system cannot support group-based access.
Target fulfilment times are:
  Standard employee access: one business day.
  New starter access: by 09:00 local time on the start date, if requested at least three business days in advance.
  Privileged or production access: two business days after all approvals are complete.
  Urgent access: only through the emergency access process.
5. Joiner, Mover, and Leaver Controls
HR is responsible for providing timely employment-status information to IT and the employee’s manager.
Joiners
  HR submits the starter record at least three business days before the start date.
  The manager requests only the access required for the employee’s initial duties.

  Accounts remain disabled until the start date unless an earlier date is approved by HR and IT.
  New users must complete security awareness training within 30 days.
Movers
  Managers must review access when an employee changes role, department, country, or reporting line.
  Access not required for the new role must be removed within one business day of the change.
  A new role must not be used to retain incompatible financial or operational permissions.
  System owners must resolve conflicting access identified by the quarterly review.
Leavers
  Involuntary termination: accounts, sessions, tokens, VPN access, and privileged credentials are disabled at the
agreed termination time.
  Planned departure: access is removed no later than the employee’s final working day.
  Company devices, security keys, and access badges must be returned.
  Shared mailbox and document ownership must be transferred to the manager.

  Company devices, security keys, and access badges must be returned.
  Shared mailbox and document ownership must be transferred to the manager.
  Service accounts, API keys, and automation owned by the leaver must be reassigned or rotated.
6. Privileged, Service, and Shared Accounts
Privileged access includes administrator, root, database owner, payment administrator, production deployment, and
security-management roles.
  Privileged access must use a separate named administrator account.
  Administrative work must not be performed from a standard account where a privileged account is available.
  Privileged credentials must be stored and rotated through CyberArk.
  Privileged sessions must be logged where technically supported.
  Permanent standing access is prohibited for production systems unless the system owner documents the
requirement.
  Just-in-time elevation should be used for cloud and infrastructure administration.

requirement.
  Just-in-time elevation should be used for cloud and infrastructure administration.
  Privileged access is reviewed monthly by the system owner and Security Operations.
Service accounts must have a named technical owner, documented purpose, system scope, and expiry or review
date.
  Interactive sign-in is disabled unless technically necessary.
  Service-account passwords and API keys must be stored in an approved secrets vault.
  Credentials must be rotated at least every 180 days, or immediately following suspected exposure.
  Service accounts must not be used for personal work or ordinary user access.
  Shared human accounts are prohibited except where a system cannot support individual accounts.
  Approved shared accounts must have a documented owner, access list, MFA where supported, and quarterly
review.

7. Access Reviews and Monitoring
System owners must review access according to the following schedule:
  Critical systems, production, payment, and customer-data platforms: quarterly.
  Other business applications: every six months.
  Privileged and emergency accounts: monthly.
  Service accounts and API credentials: quarterly.
Reviews must confirm that each user still has a valid business need, the assigned role is appropriate, and inactive or
duplicate accounts are removed. Review results and remediation evidence must be retained in ServiceNow for at
least three years.
Microsoft Entra ID, CyberArk, endpoint security tools, and key application logs are monitored by Security Operations.
Alerts may include impossible travel, repeated failed logins, MFA fatigue, unusual privilege elevation, and access
from blocked regions.
8. Lost Credentials and Suspected Compromise
Users must report suspected credential compromise immediately through the Service Desk, the Security Operations

Users must report suspected credential compromise immediately through the Service Desk, the Security Operations
mailbox, or the emergency hotline listed on the IronStore intranet.
Users must:
  Stop using the suspected credential.
  Avoid deleting messages, files, or browser history related to the event.
  Disconnect a suspected device from the network if instructed.
  Follow password-reset and MFA-re-enrolment instructions.
  Not contact an external party or investigate beyond their normal duties.
Security Operations may disable accounts, revoke sessions, rotate secrets, block indicators, and preserve evidence.
Suspected exposure of customer, payment, or employee data must be escalated to the Incident Manager and Data
Protection Officer under the Information Security Incident Response Procedure.
9. Exceptions
Exceptions must be rare, time-limited, and documented in ServiceNow. The request must include:
  The requirement and affected system.

9. Exceptions
Exceptions must be rare, time-limited, and documented in ServiceNow. The request must include:
  The requirement and affected system.
  Risk assessment and compensating controls.
  Named owner and expiry date.
  Approval from the system owner and CISO.
Exceptions expire after six months unless renewed. Critical risks may not be accepted solely by a system owner.

Roles & Responsibilities
  All users: Protect credentials, use MFA, follow approved access procedures, and report suspicious activity.
  Line managers: Request appropriate access, approve changes, and review access during role changes.
  HR: Maintain accurate joiner, mover, and leaver information.
  IT Service Desk: Verify identity, fulfil standard requests, and process account changes.
  System owners: Define roles, approve access, complete reviews, and remove unnecessary permissions.
  Security Operations: Monitor authentication activity, manage privileged controls, and investigate incidents.
  CISO: Own this policy, approve exceptions, and report material risks to the Risk Committee.
  Data Protection Officer: Advise on access to personal data and regulatory obligations.

Customer Support Knowledge Base Style Guide
Owning area: Customer_support
Last reviewed: August 2026
Document ID: CS-KB-STD-004
Policy owner: Head of Customer Support Operations
1. Purpose and Overview
This guide defines how IronStore customer support knowledge base (KB) articles are written, reviewed, published,
and maintained. It applies to customer-facing Help Centre content and internal agent guidance used across European
markets.
The objective is to provide accurate, easy-to-scan instructions that help customers resolve common issues without
contacting support. Articles must reflect current IronStore processes, product categories, delivery options, payment
methods, and country-specific requirements.
The KB is maintained in GuideHub, with operational links to Zendesk, OrderSphere, ReturnFlow, and the
IronStore Product Catalogue (IPC). GuideHub is the authoritative source for approved support content.
2. Scope
This standard applies to:

IronStore Product Catalogue (IPC). GuideHub is the authoritative source for approved support content.
2. Scope
This standard applies to:
  Public Help Centre articles, troubleshooting guides, FAQs, and policy explanations.
  Internal agent procedures, saved replies, escalation notes, and workflow instructions.
  Content created for all supported European storefronts and languages.
  New articles, major revisions, translations, and republished content.
  Content owners, subject-matter experts, translators, quality reviewers, and support agents.
This standard does not replace legal, privacy, payment-security, product-safety, or marketplace policies. Where
requirements conflict, the stricter approved policy applies.
3. Content Policy and Procedures
3.1 Article selection and ownership
Create an article when a question is:
  Asked regularly through Zendesk.
  Likely to be solved without account-specific investigation.
  Relevant to more than one product, order, or country.

  Needed to explain a change in policy, system, or customer journey.
Do not publish an article for:
  A single customer’s order or account details.
  Unconfirmed product information.
  Temporary incidents unless marked as a service notice.
  Advice that could create safety, legal, financial, or medical risk.
Each article must have one named Content Owner in GuideHub. The owner is accountable for accuracy, review
dates, and updates following process changes.
3.2 Article types and required structure
Use one of the following article types:
  How-to: Steps the customer can complete independently.
  Policy: Rules for returns, refunds, delivery, payments, or accounts.
  Troubleshooting: Checks and actions for a specific issue.
  FAQ: Short answers to common questions.
  Internal procedure: Agent-only handling and escalation instructions.
  Service notice: Time-limited information about an outage or disruption.
Use this order unless there is a clear reason to vary it:

  Service notice: Time-limited information about an outage or disruption.
Use this order unless there is a clear reason to vary it:
1. Descriptive title.
2. One-sentence summary of the customer outcome.
3. Eligibility or important conditions.
4. Numbered steps or short answer sections.
5. Exceptions and escalation guidance.
6. Related links.
7. Review metadata for internal articles.
Start with the answer. Do not open with background, apologies, or promotional language.
3.3 Titles, headings, and summaries
Titles must describe the customer’s task or question.
Preferred:
  “How to change a delivery address”
  “When will my refund be processed?”
  “What to do if your parcel arrives damaged”

Avoid:
  “Important information about orders”
  “We are here to help”
  “Delivery FAQ and other useful information”
Use sentence case for titles and headings. Keep titles below 70 characters where possible. Use headings to separate
decisions or stages, not to create unnecessary visual breaks.
The opening summary should be no more than two sentences and should state the main outcome, expected
timeframe, or key restriction.
3.4 Writing style and tone
IronStore content must be clear, neutral, practical, and respectful.
Use:
  “You can request a return within 30 days of delivery.”
  “Enter the email address used for the order.”
  “We will email you when the refund is issued.”
Avoid:
  Blame: “You entered the wrong address.”
  Unclear promises: “Your parcel should arrive soon.”
  Internal language: “The ticket has been routed to L2.”
  Excessive enthusiasm, slang, or humour.
  Legalistic wording where plain language is sufficient.

  Excessive enthusiasm, slang, or humour.
  Legalistic wording where plain language is sufficient.
Address the reader as you and IronStore as we. Use active voice and short sentences. Explain unavoidable terms at
first use, for example, “proof of delivery (POD).”
Do not use:
  All-capital words for emphasis.
  Multiple exclamation marks.
  Emoji in policy or troubleshooting content.
  “Simply,” “obviously,” “guaranteed,” or “always” unless factually exact.
  Claims that a result is certain when it depends on a carrier, bank, seller, or manufacturer.
3.5 Steps, conditions, and decision points
Write instructions as numbered steps. Each step should contain one action.

  Begin with a verb: Open, Select, Upload, Contact.
  Name the exact button or field shown in the current interface.
  Put conditions before steps where they affect eligibility.
  State what the customer should see after completing an action.
  Include the next action if a step fails.
Use bullets for lists of requirements or examples. Use tables only when they improve comparison, such as delivery
methods or refund timeframes.
For decision points, use clear “If / Then” wording:
  If the tracking page shows “Delivered” but you cannot find the parcel, contact us within 48 hours.
  If the item is damaged, do not return it before uploading photographs.
Do not direct customers to internal queues, team names, or unpublished tools.
3.6 Product, order, and policy accuracy
Before publication, verify all operational facts in the relevant system:
  Product specifications: IPC or the manufacturer’s approved data sheet.
  Order and delivery status: OrderSphere and the carrier portal.

  Product specifications: IPC or the manufacturer’s approved data sheet.
  Order and delivery status: OrderSphere and the carrier portal.
  Return eligibility: ReturnFlow and the current country policy.
  Payment status: PayCore transaction record.
  Promotions: current campaign brief in CampaignVault.
Never copy customer-specific information into a public article. Do not publish full order numbers, email addresses,
phone numbers, payment details, or screenshots containing personal data.
Timeframes must include the starting point:
  “Within 14 calendar days of delivery.”
  “Refunds are issued within five business days after inspection.”
  “Bank processing may take an additional three to seven business days.”
State the applicable country or storefront when rules differ. Do not use “Europe-wide” unless the Legal or Policy team
has confirmed that the rule is uniform.
3.7 Returns, refunds, and delivery wording
Use the approved terminology:

has confirmed that the rule is uniform.
3.7 Returns, refunds, and delivery wording
Use the approved terminology:
  Return request: customer asks to send an item back.
  Return label: shipping label issued by IronStore or a seller.
  Refund issued: IronStore has released the funds.

  Refund received: funds are visible in the customer’s account.
  Delivery estimate: expected date, not a guarantee.
  Delivery guarantee: use only where contractually confirmed.
For damaged, incorrect, or missing items, explain the evidence required and the response target. Standard guidance
is:
  Customer reports damage within 48 hours of delivery where possible.
  Customer provides photographs of the item, packaging, and shipping label.
  Support reviews the case within two business days.
  High-value claims above €250 require Customer Resolution Team review.
  Suspected fraud, repeated claims, or safety concerns go to Trust & Safety.
Do not instruct customers to dispose of an item unless the case record includes an approved disposal instruction.
3.8 Accessibility and localisation
All customer-facing content must meet IronStore’s accessibility baseline:
  Use descriptive link text, not “click here.”
  Provide meaningful alt text for essential images.

  Use descriptive link text, not “click here.”
  Provide meaningful alt text for essential images.
  Do not use colour alone to communicate status.
  Keep paragraphs to four lines or fewer on standard desktop view.
  Use headings in logical order.
  Avoid screenshots when text instructions are sufficient.
Content is initially written in International English and translated through LinguaDesk. Localisation reviewers must
check:
  Currency, date, time, and measurement formats.
  Country-specific consumer rights and delivery terms.
  Local carrier and payment names.
  Formality, terminology, and prohibited claims.
Machine or vendor translation must not be published without review by an approved language reviewer.
3.9 Links, screenshots, and system references
Use stable GuideHub links where available. Do not link directly to temporary Zendesk views, agent dashboards, or
personal documents.
Screenshots must:
  Show only the relevant area.

  Use the current interface.
  Exclude personal data, internal IDs, and browser notifications.
  Include a short caption or alt text.
  Be reviewed whenever the interface changes.
Broken links, outdated images, or missing translations are content defects and must be corrected within five
business days of identification.
3.10 Review, approval, and publication
The Content Owner completes the draft and records the source of each policy or operational claim. Required
approval depends on content type:
  Standard how-to or FAQ: Support Knowledge Manager.
  Returns, refunds, delivery, or payment policy: Support Operations Manager and relevant Policy Owner.
  Privacy or personal-data content: Privacy Counsel.
  Product safety or regulated products: Product Compliance Manager.
  Country-specific legal wording: Local Market Lead.
The Knowledge Manager publishes approved content in GuideHub and records:
  Owner and approving roles.
  Applicable markets and languages.

The Knowledge Manager publishes approved content in GuideHub and records:
  Owner and approving roles.
  Applicable markets and languages.
  Publication date.
  Next review date.
  Related systems or policy references.
Standard articles are reviewed every six months. Payment, privacy, safety, and legal articles are reviewed every
three months. Articles affected by a process or system change must be reviewed before the change goes live.
Agents should flag inaccurate or unclear content using the “Report KB issue” form in Zendesk. Critical errors
affecting refunds, safety, privacy, or customer eligibility must be escalated to the Team Lead immediately and
corrected or temporarily unpublished within one business day.
4. Roles and Responsibilities
  Support Knowledge Manager: Owns this standard, publishing controls, audits, and reporting.
  Content Owner: Drafts, maintains, and reviews assigned articles.
  Subject-Matter Expert: Confirms operational or product accuracy.

  Content Owner: Drafts, maintains, and reviews assigned articles.
  Subject-Matter Expert: Confirms operational or product accuracy.

  Support Agent: Uses approved content and reports defects; does not create unapproved customer policy.

  Policy, Legal, Privacy, or Compliance Owner: Approves specialist content within their remit.

Customer Support Escalation Procedures
Owning area: Customer_support
Last reviewed: August 2026
Document ID: CS-POL-014
Version: 3.2
Applies to: IronStore customer support operations across Europe
1. Purpose and Overview
This procedure defines how IronStore identifies, manages, and escalates customer contacts that cannot be resolved
through standard frontline support. It is intended to ensure consistent decisions, timely ownership, and appropriate
protection of customer, payment, product, and company information.
Escalation is required when a case involves material customer impact, operational risk, legal or regulatory
considerations, reputational risk, or a resolution outside the agent’s authority. Escalation does not remove ownership
from the original agent unless a receiving team formally accepts the case.
The procedure applies to contacts received through email, telephone, chat, social media, marketplace messaging,
and the IronStore Help Centre.

3. Policy Statement
IronStore support cases must be resolved at the lowest appropriate level, using approved tools and decision limits.
Escalations must be based on documented facts rather than customer status, personal preference, or pressure from
a third party.
Agents must:
  Record all material facts in Zendesk before escalating.
  Use the correct escalation category and priority.
  Avoid promising an outcome that requires another team’s approval.
  Provide the customer with a realistic next-update time.
  Protect personal data by using approved internal systems only.
  Continue monitoring the case until ownership is accepted or resolution is confirmed.
No employee may disclose internal investigation details, fraud rules, warehouse controls, security information, or
another customer’s data.
4. Standard Escalation Procedure
4.1 Initial assessment
The assigned agent must complete the following checks:
1. Confirm the customer’s identity using the approved verification steps.

The assigned agent must complete the following checks:

2. Review the full contact history, order record, payment status, and delivery events.
3. Check for duplicate tickets, open complaints, chargebacks, or previous escalations.
4. Identify the customer’s country, applicable language, currency, and service terms.
5. Determine whether the case is routine, priority, urgent, or critical.
6. Record the reason for escalation in Zendesk using the relevant macro.
If information is missing, the agent should request it before escalating unless delay could increase customer or
business risk.
4.2 Escalation record requirements
Every escalation must include:

Do not copy full payment card numbers, passwords, identity documents, or unnecessary personal information into

5. Escalation Categories and Routing
5.1 Order, delivery, and warehouse issues
Escalate to Logistics Operations when:

  A shipment is held by customs or repeatedly misrouted.

5.2 Refunds, payments, and chargebacks
Escalate to Payments Operations when:

Agents may approve refunds only within their role limit and the Refund Authority Matrix CS-FIN-006. Refunds

Do not advise a customer to withdraw a chargeback before the case has been reviewed by Payments Operations.
5.3 Fraud and account security
Escalate immediately to Trust & Safety when there is evidence of:
  Account takeover or unauthorised password or email changes.
  Unrecognised orders, payment methods, or delivery addresses.

  Account takeover or unauthorised password or email changes.

  Multiple accounts using suspicious vouchers or referral credits.

Use the Fraud Escalation form in Zendesk. Do not accuse the customer of fraud or disclose detection criteria. Apply

Suspected personal data breaches must also be reported through Security Hub within 30 minutes. Customer

5.4 Product safety and quality
Escalate to Product Compliance as P1 or P2 when a customer reports:

  A product defect that could cause injury or property damage.

  A product defect that could cause injury or property damage.
  Suspected counterfeit, unsafe, or incorrectly labelled goods.

Capture the product name, SKU, batch or serial number, purchase date, customer description, and photographs if

Route formal legal notices, data-subject rights concerns, consumer authority requests, and threats of litigation to
Legal & Compliance. Use the customer’s country queue and preserve the original wording. Do not interpret

an immediate and credible threat.
