Version: 3.2
Last reviewed: August 2026
Approved by: Director of Customer Operations
Applies to: IronStore EU operating companies and customer-support channels
1. Purpose and Overview
This policy defines how IronStore receives, investigates, and resolves customer complaints and refund requests. It is
intended to provide consistent outcomes, protect customer rights, and ensure that cases are recorded accurately for
operational and regulatory reporting.
IronStore sells consumer products across Europe, including electronics, home essentials, clothing, outdoor
equipment, beauty products, and other categories. Refund eligibility may differ by product type, fulfilment route,
payment method, country, and applicable consumer law. Where local law provides a stronger customer right than this
policy, the legal requirement takes precedence.
2. Scope
This policy applies to:

policy, the legal requirement takes precedence.
2. Scope
This policy applies to:
  Orders placed through IronStore websites, mobile applications, and approved marketplace channels.
  Customer contacts received by email, web form, live chat, telephone, and social-care channels.
  Refunds for cancelled orders, returns, damaged or faulty goods, failed delivery, duplicate charges, and service
errors.
  Complaints about products, delivery, payment, customer service, sellers, or fulfilment partners.
  Cases handled by Customer Support, Payments Operations, Warehouse Operations, and Marketplace Support.
This policy does not replace product-specific safety procedures, payment-provider rules, or country-specific legal
guidance.
3. Policy Statement
IronStore will:
  Acknowledge complaints and refund requests promptly.
  Apply the same decision rules to comparable cases.
  Provide clear explanations when a request is declined or only partly approved.

  Apply the same decision rules to comparable cases.
  Provide clear explanations when a request is declined or only partly approved.
  Record all material actions in the approved case-management system.

  Protect customer data and limit access to staff with a business need.
  Escalate safety, legal, fraud, and executive-risk matters without delay.
  Pay approved refunds to the original payment method unless an approved exception applies.
Customer Support must not promise a refund before eligibility has been checked, except where a published
automatic-refund rule clearly applies.
4. Standard Refund Procedure
4.1 Case intake and verification
The agent must locate the order in ServiceHub, using the order number, verified email address, or approved
marketplace reference.
Before discussing order details or issuing a refund, the agent must verify at least two approved identifiers, such as:
  Customer email address and order number.
  Delivery postcode and product description.
  Payment token suffix and order date.
Agents must not request or record full card numbers, CVV codes, account passwords, or unnecessary identity
documents.
The agent records:
  Contact channel and date.

documents.
The agent records:
  Contact channel and date.
  Customer’s stated reason.
  Affected item, quantity, and order line.
  Evidence supplied, including photographs or carrier information.
  Requested outcome and applicable policy reason code.
4.2 Eligibility assessment
The agent checks the following in ServiceHub and OrderCore:
1. Order status and fulfilment route.
2. Delivery date or confirmed cancellation date.
3. Return-window status.
4. Product category restrictions.
5. Previous refunds, replacements, or related complaints.
6. Payment settlement status and refund capability.
For standard consumer returns, the applicable country return period is shown in the customer’s order terms. Unless a
longer legal or commercial period applies, unopened and resalable goods are accepted within 30 calendar days of

delivery. Product-specific exceptions include:
  Personalised goods: normally non-returnable unless faulty.
  Sealed hygiene or beauty products: non-returnable after seal removal where permitted by law.
  Digital content: subject to acceptance and commencement rules.
  Large or hazardous goods: collection may be required.
  Marketplace items: the marketplace seller’s approved return workflow applies.
A faulty, damaged, incorrect, or materially misdescribed item must not be rejected solely because the standard return
window has expired. The agent follows the applicable statutory remedy process and consults Returns Operations
where the remedy is unclear.
4.3 Evidence and inspection
Evidence should be proportionate to the issue. Agents may request:
  Clear photographs of damaged packaging or product.
  A short video for intermittent faults where practical.
  Carrier damage details or delivery confirmation.
  Serial number or batch information for controlled products.

  Carrier damage details or delivery confirmation.
  Serial number or batch information for controlled products.
Do not request evidence that is unsafe, unreasonable, or already available in IronStore systems. For low-value items,
the No-Return Refund Matrix may permit a refund without physical return.
The current matrix is:
  Up to €25: agent may refund or replace without approval when evidence is sufficient.
  €25.01–€150: team-lead approval is required for a no-return refund unless an automatic rule applies.
  Over €150: Returns Operations or Payments Operations approval is required.
  Any safety-related product: immediate escalation, regardless of value.
4.4 Refund approval and processing
The agent selects the correct reason code and enters the amount in ServiceHub. The system performs
duplicate-refund and open-dispute checks before submission.
Approval requirements:
  Up to €150: trained agent within documented authority.
  €150.01–€500: Customer Support Team Lead.

Approval requirements:
  Up to €150: trained agent within documented authority.
  €150.01–€500: Customer Support Team Lead.
  Above €500: Customer Operations Manager and Finance Operations.
  Any goodwill amount above €50: Team Lead approval.
  Any refund outside policy: Customer Operations Manager approval, with rationale recorded.

Refunds are normally returned to the original payment method. Finance Operations handles exceptions such as
expired cards, closed accounts, cash-on-delivery payments, or payment-provider limitations.
Expected processing times after approval:
  Card and digital wallet refunds: usually 3–7 business days.
  Bank-transfer refunds: usually 3–5 business days after bank details are validated.
  Marketplace refunds: according to the marketplace settlement timetable.
  Refunds awaiting warehouse inspection: decision within five business days of receipt unless a specialist
assessment is required.
The customer must receive a confirmation showing the approved amount, refund method, and expected processing
time.
4.5 Partial refunds, replacements, and goodwill
A partial refund may be offered where the customer keeps an item with a minor, documented defect and the solution
is lawful and commercially appropriate. The amount must reflect the issue and must not be used to avoid a statutory
remedy.

is lawful and commercially appropriate. The amount must reflect the issue and must not be used to avoid a statutory
remedy.
Replacement is preferred when:
  The item is unavailable for immediate refund processing.
  The customer requests a replacement and stock is available.
  Replacement is operationally safer or faster than repair.
Goodwill credits are discretionary and must not be described as a legal entitlement. Agents must not issue goodwill to
close a complaint involving safety, discrimination, suspected fraud, or a serious data incident; those cases require
escalation.
5. Complaint Handling Procedure
5.1 Definition and acknowledgement
A complaint is any expression of dissatisfaction that requires a response, investigation, or corrective action. The
agent creates a Complaint case in ServiceHub rather than treating it only as a standard enquiry.
The acknowledgement should include:
  Complaint reference number.
  Summary of the issue as understood.

The acknowledgement should include:
  Complaint reference number.
  Summary of the issue as understood.
  Named owner or responsible team.
  Expected next update date.
  Any information still required from the customer.
Target timeframes:

  Acknowledge within one business day.
  Provide a substantive response within five business days.
  Resolve standard complaints within ten business days where practical.
  Notify the customer if an investigation will take longer and provide a revised date.
5.2 Investigation and resolution
The case owner reviews order history, contact notes, warehouse scans, carrier events, payment records, and
relevant seller communications. Staff must avoid speculative statements and distinguish confirmed facts from
assumptions.
Possible outcomes include:
  Explanation with no further action.
  Refund, replacement, repair, or return arrangement.
  Delivery investigation with the carrier or fulfilment centre.
  Product or seller escalation.
  Process correction and customer apology.
  Formal referral to Legal, Compliance, or Product Safety.
The final response must be clear, respectful, and specific. It should state:
  What was reviewed.
  The decision and reason.

The final response must be clear, respectful, and specific. It should state:
  What was reviewed.
  The decision and reason.
  Any refund or corrective action.
  Expected completion date.
  How the customer may request a review.
5.3 Escalation triggers
Immediate escalation through the Risk & Escalations queue is required for:
  Injury, fire, electric shock, contamination, or suspected product safety risk.
  Allegations of discrimination, harassment, or abusive staff conduct.
  Threats of legal action, regulator contact, media exposure, or executive complaint.
  Suspected payment fraud, account takeover, or organised refund abuse.
  Repeated delivery failures affecting multiple customers.
  Requests from law enforcement, regulators, or data-protection authorities.
  Vulnerable-customer concerns requiring specialist support.
Product Safety cases must also be logged in IncidentTrack within four hours. Staff must not advise customers to

Product Safety cases must also be logged in IncidentTrack within four hours. Staff must not advise customers to
continue using a potentially unsafe product.

5.4 Review and deadlock
If a customer disputes the outcome, the case is reassigned to a Team Lead or Complaints Specialist who was not the
original decision-maker where possible. The review should be completed within five business days.
A second review may change the outcome only when new evidence, a policy error, or an exceptional circumstance is
identified. Repeated contacts about the same resolved matter may be managed under the Reasonable Contact
Standard, but genuine new information must always be assessed.
6. Fraud, Abuse, and Chargebacks
Refund abuse indicators may include repeated claims of non-delivery, inconsistent damage evidence, serial-number
mismatches, or multiple accounts linked to the same payment instrument. Agents must not accuse customers or
disclose fraud-detection rules.
Suspected abuse is referred to Trust & Payments using the reason code REFUND-RISK. Legitimate customer cases
must continue to receive a timely response while checks are performed.

must continue to receive a timely response while checks are performed.
When a card chargeback is received:
  Payments Operations owns the dispute response.
  Customer Support must not issue a duplicate refund without approval.
  Relevant delivery, refund, and communication evidence must be preserved.
  The case outcome must be linked to the original ServiceHub record.
7. Records, Reporting, and Data Retention
All decisions, approvals, customer communications, and evidence references must be stored in ServiceHub.
Attachments containing sensitive information must use the restricted evidence repository, not personal drives or email
inboxes.
Customer data is handled according to the Privacy and Records Retention Standard. Staff must not export case
lists unless approved for a defined operational purpose.
Customer Operations reviews monthly:
  Refund rate by category, seller, country, and reason code.
  Complaint volume and ageing.
  Repeat contacts and reopened cases.

  Refund rate by category, seller, country, and reason code.
  Complaint volume and ageing.
  Repeat contacts and reopened cases.
  Approval exceptions and goodwill spend.
  Chargebacks, fraud referrals, and safety incidents.
  Compliance with acknowledgement and resolution targets.
Trends requiring action are assigned to the relevant process owner and tracked in the monthly Customer Experience
review.

8. Roles and Responsibilities
  Customer Support Agents: Verify identity, assess eligibility, document cases, and communicate decisions.
  Team Leads: Approve defined refunds, review escalations, coach agents, and monitor ageing.
  Complaints Specialists: Own formal complaints and independent reviews.
  Returns Operations: Assess returned goods, faults, collections, and warehouse exceptions.
  Payments Operations: Process payment exceptions, chargebacks, and settlement issues.

  Finance Operations: Reconcile refunds, goodwill spend, and payment-provider exceptions.

consumer goods.

collective agreements, and formally adopted country addenda take precedence where they provide different or
stronger rights.

1. Purpose and Overview
This policy explains how IronStore employees request, record, approve, and manage annual leave and other
absences. It supports consistent workforce planning while ensuring compliance with applicable employment law in
each country where IronStore operates.
Local statutory requirements, collective agreements, and employment contracts take precedence over this policy.
Employees should contact People Operations if a local rule differs from the process described below.
2. Scope
This policy applies to:
  All IronStore employees, including permanent, fixed-term, part-time, and probationary employees.
  Employees working from IronStore offices, fulfilment sites, customer service centres, and approved remote
locations.
  Line managers responsible for approving leave or managing attendance.

locations.
  Line managers responsible for approving leave or managing attendance.
  Agency workers and contractors only where their contract or local agreement expressly adopts these
procedures.
The policy covers:
  Annual or holiday leave.
  Public holidays and company closure days.
  Sickness absence.
  Family, parental, compassionate, and other statutory leave.
  Unpaid leave and extended absence.
  Return-to-work and absence records.
3. Policy Statement
IronStore provides leave in accordance with local law, the employee’s contract, and approved company benefits.
Employees are expected to take their full statutory annual leave entitlement unless local law permits a lawful
carryover or other arrangement.

Leave must be requested in advance through PeopleHub, IronStore’s HR system. Leave is not confirmed until
approved by the employee’s line manager, except where an absence is unexpected or legally protected.
Employees must:
  Submit accurate leave dates and absence reasons where required.
  Follow notice and documentation requirements.
  Keep their manager informed of changes.
  Avoid working for IronStore while recorded as absent or on leave, unless specifically authorised.
  Return to work on the agreed date.
Managers must apply this policy consistently and should not unreasonably delay or refuse leave requests.
4. Annual Leave
4.1 Entitlement
Annual leave entitlement is shown in the employee’s PeopleHub profile and employment contract. It may vary by:
  Country of employment.
  Contractual working hours and working pattern.
  Length of service.
  Collective agreement or local benefit scheme.

  Country of employment.
  Contractual working hours and working pattern.
  Length of service.
  Collective agreement or local benefit scheme.
Part-time employees receive a pro-rated entitlement where applicable. Public holidays are handled according to the
employee’s work location and local law.
The leave year runs from 1 January to 31 December, unless a local entity has an approved alternative.
4.2 Request and Approval
Employees should submit annual leave requests through PeopleHub:
  At least 10 calendar days before leave of one to five working days.
  At least 20 calendar days before leave exceeding five working days.
  As early as possible for peak periods, including July–August, year-end, and major local holidays.
Managers should respond within five working days. Approval depends on operational coverage, customer
commitments, fulfilment schedules, and previously approved leave.

commitments, fulfilment schedules, and previously approved leave.
Managers may propose alternative dates where several employees request the same period. Business needs must
be assessed fairly and should not routinely prevent employees from taking their entitlement.
Leave may not be treated as approved solely because a request has been submitted or because a manager has not
responded.

4.3 Taking and Carrying Leave
Employees should normally take leave in blocks that support adequate rest. Managers may require leave to be
scheduled where necessary to meet legal minimums, following consultation with the employee and People
Operations.
Unused leave:
  Expires at the end of the leave year unless carryover is permitted by local law, contract, or written approval.
  May be carried over when the employee could not take it because of protected leave, long-term sickness, or a
documented business restriction.
  Must be recorded in PeopleHub using the correct carryover category.
People Operations will issue reminders during the year. Employees and managers remain jointly responsible for
preventing excessive balances.
4.4 Cancelling or Changing Leave
Employees should amend or cancel approved leave in PeopleHub before the scheduled start date. Changes are
subject to manager approval.

Employees should amend or cancel approved leave in PeopleHub before the scheduled start date. Changes are
subject to manager approval.
IronStore may cancel approved leave only for significant and unforeseen operational reasons. The manager must
consult the employee, provide reasonable notice where possible, and reimburse or address unavoidable costs where
required by local law.

Public holidays are determined by the employee’s official work location. Employees working across borders must
confirm the applicable calendar with People Operations.
IronStore may designate limited company closure days, such as 24 December through 31 December, for selected
offices or teams. Closure arrangements will be communicated before the relevant leave year and will specify whether
the days are:

Employees who cannot work because of illness or injury must notify their manager and record the absence in

The manager must be informed of any significant change in the expected return date. Employees should provide a fit

their country. People Operations may request an Occupational Health assessment where lawful and proportionate.

A manager should hold a brief welfare check after approximately five working days, then agree an appropriate
contact schedule. Contact must be supportive and must not pressure the employee to return before medically fit.

  Expected timescales and relevant documentation.
  Workplace adjustments or phased return options.
  Pay, benefits, and statutory reporting.
  Any legal or occupational health requirements.

People Operations will confirm entitlement, pay treatment, notice dates, and any required handover. Employees must

additional statutory or discretionary leave considered by the manager and People Operations.

Requests are handled sensitively. Evidence should be requested only where necessary.

Approval requires the line manager and People Operations. Requests exceeding 20 working days also require
approval from the relevant department director.
Before approval, People Operations will explain effects on salary, benefits, pension or social insurance, holiday
accrual, and service dates. Unpaid leave must not be used to conceal sickness absence or work for a competitor.

PeopleHub is the official record for leave and absence. Payroll uses approved records for salary, statutory payments,

9. Recording, Pay, and Privacy
PeopleHub is the official record for leave and absence. Payroll uses approved records for salary, statutory payments,

Absence information is personal data. IronStore processes it only for employment administration, legal compliance,

10. Return to Work
Following sickness absence, the employee should complete a return-to-work check-in with their manager within three
working days. The discussion should cover:

  Any temporary adjustments or support.

working days. The discussion should cover:

agreed.

Purpose and Overview
This workflow defines how IronStore requests, reviews, approves, records, and monitors expenditure. It applies to
operating costs, capital expenditure, marketing spend, technology investments, logistics projects, supplier
commitments, and other purchases made on behalf of the company.
The workflow is intended to ensure that spending is:
  Within an approved budget or properly justified as unplanned.
  Supported by a clear business need and documented supplier terms.
  Approved by the correct budget owner and financial authority.
  Compliant with procurement, tax, legal, information security, and delegated-authority requirements.
  Recorded accurately in IronStore’s financial systems before a commitment is made.

  Recorded accurately in IronStore’s financial systems before a commitment is made.
No employee may commit IronStore funds, sign a supplier order, or instruct a supplier to begin work before the
required approvals are complete.
Scope
This policy covers:
  Purchase orders, statements of work, subscriptions, advertising commitments, and supplier contracts.
  One-time and recurring expenditure, including renewals and automatic extensions.
  Capital expenditure, such as warehouse equipment, software development, fixtures, and infrastructure.
  Employee expenses where the cost was not already covered by an approved purchase order.
  Spend made by IronStore legal entities in the EU, UK, Switzerland, and other European operating markets.
This policy does not replace:
  The Procurement and Supplier Due Diligence Standard (PROC-STD-003).
  The Delegation of Authority Matrix (FIN-MAT-002).
  Local tax, employment, data protection, or statutory accounting requirements.

  The Delegation of Authority Matrix (FIN-MAT-002).
  Local tax, employment, data protection, or statutory accounting requirements.
Where local law or a customer-contract obligation is stricter, the stricter requirement applies.

Policy Statement
All expenditure must have:
1. A named business owner.
2. An approved cost centre and, where applicable, project code.
3. A documented commercial rationale.
4. A valid approval in Coupa, IronStore’s purchasing and approval platform.
5. A purchase order or approved contract before goods or services are ordered.
6. A matching invoice, receipt, or delivery confirmation before payment.
Approvals may not be split across invoices, suppliers, projects, or accounting periods to avoid an approval threshold.
A commitment includes the full expected value, including extensions, implementation fees, minimum usage charges,
taxes that cannot be recovered, and the initial contract term.
Approvers must not approve their own expenses, their own compensation, or expenditure from which they receive a
personal benefit. Finance may reject, hold, or escalate transactions that do not meet this policy.

Budget Approval Procedure
1. Define the request
The requester creates a Spend Request in Coupa before contacting a supplier or confirming an order. The request
must include:
  Description of the product, service, or project.
  Business purpose and expected outcome.
  Total committed value in EUR, excluding recoverable VAT.
  Contract term, renewal date, and cancellation terms.
  Supplier name or proposed sourcing approach.
  Cost centre, general ledger category, and project code.
  Expected delivery date and payment schedule.
  Confirmation that the cost is in the approved annual budget.
For foreign-currency commitments, the requester records the EUR equivalent using the monthly Finance planning
rate in NetSuite. Finance may update the value using the contracted exchange rate before final approval.
2. Check budget availability

rate in NetSuite. Finance may update the value using the contracted exchange rate before final approval.
2. Check budget availability
The budget owner checks the request against the current plan in Anaplan and the actuals in Oracle NetSuite.
The request must identify one of the following:

  Budgeted spend: Covered by the current approved plan.
  Budget transfer: Covered by another cost centre or project and requiring a documented reallocation.
  Unplanned spend: Not included in the approved plan and requiring additional approval.
  Renewal spend: A recurring commitment that must be reassessed before renewal, even if previously approved.
Budget availability does not itself authorise the purchase. Approval must still follow the thresholds below.
3. Obtain commercial and specialist review
Before financial approval, the requester obtains the relevant reviews:
  Procurement: Required for new suppliers, competitive sourcing, or spend above €25,000.
  Legal: Required for contracts, data processing, intellectual property, exclusivity, unusual liability, or
non-standard terms.
  Information Security: Required for software, hosted services, integrations, customer data, or access to
IronStore systems.

  Tax: Required for cross-border arrangements, unusual VAT treatment, customs, royalties, or withholding-tax
exposure.
  People Team: Required for recruitment agencies, contractors, employee benefits, or workforce-related
services.
Coupa routes required reviews based on category, supplier, entity, and value. Reviewers record conditions or
exceptions directly in the request.
4. Apply approval thresholds
Approval thresholds are based on the total expected commitment per supplier and business need. The following
minimum chain applies:
  Up to €5,000: Cost centre owner.
  €5,001–€25,000: Cost centre owner and department director.
  €25,001–€100,000: Department director and regional Finance Business Partner.
  €100,001–€500,000: Executive sponsor, Finance Director, and Procurement Director.

  €100,001–€500,000: Executive sponsor, Finance Director, and Procurement Director.
  Above €500,000: Executive sponsor, CFO, and CEO or designated Executive Committee member.
Additional requirements:
  Capital expenditure above €50,000: Finance Business Partner and CFO delegate must confirm the asset
classification, useful life, and capital budget.
  Marketing commitments above €100,000: Chief Marketing Officer or delegate must approve the commercial
plan and performance measures.
  Technology commitments above €100,000: Chief Technology Officer or delegate must approve architecture,
security, and implementation capacity.

  New or renewed contracts with a term exceeding 36 months: Legal and CFO delegate approval are

  Multi-year commitments: Approval is based on the full contract value, not the annual instalment.
An approver may delegate authority only through the approved Coupa delegation function. Email approval is not

5. Complete sourcing and contracting
Procurement determines the sourcing method:
  Up to €25,000: documented price or market check where practical.
  €25,001–€100,000: normally at least two competitive quotations.
  Above €100,000: normally a formal tender with at least three qualified suppliers.
A sole-source or emergency exception requires a written justification in Coupa and Procurement approval. The
justification must explain the supplier dependency, urgency, market constraints, or technical compatibility.

justification must explain the supplier dependency, urgency, market constraints, or technical compatibility.
Only authorised signatories may execute supplier contracts. A purchase order is not a substitute for a contract where
legal, data protection, or commercial terms require a signed agreement.
6. Issue the purchase order
After all approvals are complete, Procurement or the authorised requester converts the approved request into a
purchase order. The supplier must receive the purchase order before delivery or service commencement.
The purchase order must state:
  Legal entity and billing address.
  Supplier details and tax registration information.
  Approved value and currency.
  Payment terms and delivery requirements.
  Cost centre, project code, and requester.
  Applicable contract or statement of work reference.
Invoices without a valid purchase order are placed on hold unless Finance approves a documented exception.
7. Monitor delivery and invoice matching

7. Monitor delivery and invoice matching
The requester confirms receipt of goods or completion of services in Coupa. Accounts Payable performs a three-way
match between:
1. Approved purchase order.
2. Receipt or service confirmation.
3. Supplier invoice.

Discrepancies are resolved by the requester, Procurement, or supplier. Accounts Payable does not amend an
approved order to conceal an overspend.
The requester must review recurring services at least 30 days before renewal. The review must confirm continued
business need, supplier performance, pricing, user volumes, and cancellation deadlines.
Unplanned, Urgent, and Exceptional Spend
Unplanned spend follows the normal approval chain and must identify the funding source. Finance may require a
forecast update or budget transfer before approval.
Urgent spend is limited to situations involving:
  Customer, employee, or physical safety.
  Material interruption to fulfilment, payment, logistics, or core systems.
  Legal or regulatory deadlines.
  Significant risk of financial loss if action is delayed.
The requester must obtain verbal approval from the relevant executive or Finance leader and document it in Coupa

The requester must obtain verbal approval from the relevant executive or Finance leader and document it in Coupa
within two business days. Procurement and Legal must be informed as soon as practicable. Convenience, supplier
pressure, missed planning deadlines, or a favourable discount do not qualify as urgent circumstances.
Petty cash, personal cards, or direct supplier payments must not be used to bypass this workflow. Repeated
exceptions may result in suspension of purchasing access or disciplinary action.
Roles and Responsibilities
  Requester: Defines the need, provides accurate information, monitors delivery, and confirms receipt.
  Budget owner: Confirms business priority, budget availability, and value for money.
  Department director: Reviews material departmental commitments and operational impact.
  Finance Business Partner: Validates funding, accounting treatment, forecast impact, and thresholds.

  Finance Business Partner: Validates funding, accounting treatment, forecast impact, and thresholds.
  Procurement: Manages sourcing, supplier onboarding, competitive bids, and purchase orders.
  Legal: Reviews contractual, regulatory, liability, intellectual property, and data protection matters.
  Information Security: Assesses technology, access, hosting, and security risks.
  Accounts Payable: Performs invoice controls, tax checks, and payment processing.
  CFO: Owns this policy, approves designated high-value commitments, and resolves escalations.
  Internal Audit: Tests compliance and reports material control failures to the Audit Committee.
Records, Controls, and Reporting
Coupa is the system of record for purchase approvals, sourcing evidence, purchase orders, and exceptions. NetSuite

budgets, forecasts, and approved planning assumptions.

Records must be retained for at least seven years, or longer where local law, a contract, or a litigation hold requires it.
Finance publishes a monthly report covering:

  Open purchase orders and unused commitments.
  Unplanned and exception spend.
  Contract renewals due within 90 days.
  Invoices received without purchase orders.
  Approval breaches and overdue remediation.

Shipping & Delivery SLA Policy
Owning area: Deliveries
Last reviewed: August 2026
Policy ID: DEL-SLA-004
Effective date: 1 September 2026
Policy owner: Director of Delivery Operations
1. Purpose and Overview
This policy defines IronStore’s delivery service levels, operational requirements, escalation rules, and customer
communication standards for orders shipped within the European Economic Area (EEA), the United Kingdom, and
Switzerland.
The policy applies from order release to confirmed delivery, including carrier handover, tracking, failed delivery,
delays, damage, and loss. It establishes minimum service expectations for fulfilment centres, marketplace sellers,
carriers, Customer Care, and Delivery Operations.
Service levels are measured using timestamps from IronStore’s Order Management System (OMS), Warehouse
Management System (WMS), and carrier tracking feeds. Unless a product page or checkout promise states a stricter

Management System (WMS), and carrier tracking feeds. Unless a product page or checkout promise states a stricter
commitment, this policy sets the applicable minimum standard.
2. Scope
This policy covers:
  Orders placed through the IronStore website, mobile application, and approved marketplace channels.
  Standard, express, scheduled, click-and-collect, and bulky-item deliveries.
  Shipments dispatched from IronStore fulfilment centres and approved merchant locations.
  Delivery activity in EEA countries, the UK, and Switzerland.
  Carrier performance, customer notifications, exception handling, and delivery claims.
This policy does not cover:
  Digital products, services, subscriptions, or gift-card-only orders.
  Deliveries to restricted territories, military addresses, or unsupported forwarding services.
  Delays caused solely by customer-requested changes after dispatch.
  Product-specific installation or assembly services unless included in the order confirmation.

  Product-specific installation or assembly services unless included in the order confirmation.
3. Policy Statement

IronStore must provide a delivery promise that is achievable, location-specific, and based on current inventory,
fulfilment capacity, carrier service, and cut-off times. The promise shown at checkout is the customer-facing SLA.
Orders must be delivered within the promised window unless an approved exception applies. When a delivery risk is
identified, IronStore must notify the customer promptly and provide a revised date or an available resolution.
The standard delivery target is measured in calendar days from payment approval and order release. Public holidays,
carrier non-operating days, and customer-requested delivery holds are excluded where stated at checkout.
4. Delivery Service Levels
4.1 Standard parcel delivery
For in-stock products shipped from an IronStore fulfilment centre:
  Domestic delivery: 2–4 working days after dispatch.
  Cross-border EEA delivery: 3–7 working days after dispatch.
  UK and Switzerland delivery: 4–8 working days after dispatch.

  Cross-border EEA delivery: 3–7 working days after dispatch.
  UK and Switzerland delivery: 4–8 working days after dispatch.
  Dispatch target: within one working day of payment approval.
  Orders placed after the published daily cut-off are treated as placed on the next working day.
The checkout promise may be longer for remote areas, customs-controlled destinations, or seller-fulfilled products.
4.2 Express delivery
Where offered:
  Dispatch target: same working day for orders placed before the local cut-off.
  Domestic delivery: next working day after dispatch.
  Cross-border delivery: 1–3 working days after dispatch.
  Express service must not be offered where carrier capacity, product dimensions, or destination restrictions
make the promise unreliable.
Express eligibility is determined by the Delivery Promise Engine and may not be manually overridden without
approval from the Regional Delivery Manager.
4.3 Bulky and special-handling orders

approval from the Regional Delivery Manager.
4.3 Bulky and special-handling orders
Bulky products, including furniture, large appliances, fitness equipment, and selected outdoor products, use a
scheduled delivery service:
  Customer contact within two working days of order release.
  Delivery appointment offered within 5–12 working days, subject to postcode and capacity.
  Two-person delivery, room-of-choice, installation, or disposal services must be confirmed in the order record.
  Failed appointments caused by the customer may incur a rebooking charge where disclosed before purchase.

Split orders may arrive in separate consignments. The customer must receive a clear explanation of the expected
sequence and any additional delivery charges before payment.
5. Operational Procedures
5.1 Order release and fulfilment
The OMS releases orders to the WMS or approved merchant channel after payment approval and fraud screening.
Fulfilment teams must:
  Confirm stock allocation within four hours during operating hours.
  Pick, pack, and manifest standard orders within the applicable dispatch target.
  Use packaging appropriate to product dimensions, fragility, and regulatory requirements.
  Scan the parcel at pack station and carrier handover.
  Ensure the tracking number is linked to the correct order and customer notification.
If stock becomes unavailable after checkout, the fulfilment centre must place the order in “inventory exception” status
within two hours. Customer Care must be notified before the promised dispatch date.
5.2 Carrier handover and tracking

within two hours. Customer Care must be notified before the promised dispatch date.
5.2 Carrier handover and tracking
Approved carriers must receive parcels against a manifest or electronic handover record. The first carrier scan should
occur within 24 hours of manifest creation.
Delivery Operations monitors:
  No-scan shipments exceeding 36 hours.
  Shipments with no movement for 48 hours.
  Repeated failed delivery attempts.
  Carrier status codes indicating damage, address problems, customs holds, or return to sender.
The Carrier Performance Dashboard in Looker is the primary reporting source. Manual spreadsheets may be used
only during system outages and must be reconciled within two working days.
5.3 Customer communication
The following messages must be sent through the Notification Service:
  Order confirmation after successful payment.
  Dispatch confirmation with carrier name and tracking link.
  Out-for-delivery notification where supported.

  Dispatch confirmation with carrier name and tracking link.
  Out-for-delivery notification where supported.
  Delivery confirmation or collection-ready message.

  Delay, failed-delivery, or address-action notification when required.
A delivery delay of more than one working day against the checkout promise requires proactive customer contact.
The message must include:
  Current shipment status.
  Revised estimated delivery date.
  Available customer options.
  Customer Care contact route.
Customer Care must not promise compensation, replacement, or refund outside the approved matrix without the
required approval.
5.4 Address changes and delivery holds
Before dispatch, address corrections may be made by Customer Care after customer verification. After dispatch:
  Address changes must be requested through the carrier where supported.
  Delivery holds require carrier confirmation and must be recorded in the OMS.
  Any additional carrier charge requires customer approval before acceptance.
  Fraud, account takeover, or high-value address changes must be referred to Trust & Safety.

  Fraud, account takeover, or high-value address changes must be referred to Trust & Safety.
A customer-requested change resets the delivery commitment where the revised date is shown or explicitly accepted
by the customer.
5.5 Failed delivery and returns
For a first failed attempt, the carrier should provide a re-delivery, collection-point, or customer-rescheduling option
where available.
IronStore must review shipments after:
  Two failed delivery attempts.
  Five calendar days at a collection point.
  A “return to sender” scan.
  An address exception that remains unresolved for 24 hours.
If a parcel is returned because of carrier error, IronStore must offer a replacement or refund without charging the
customer. If the customer supplied an incomplete or incorrect address, resolution follows the Returns and Refunds
Policy.
6. Exceptions, Claims, and Compensation
6.1 Service exceptions

The following may suspend or extend the SLA:
  Severe weather, flooding, natural disasters, or major transport disruption.
  Customs inspection or missing import information.
  Regulatory restrictions or border closures.
  Carrier network outage or industrial action.
  Customer-requested changes or unavailable delivery access.
  Incorrect, incomplete, or refused delivery address.
Delivery Operations must classify exceptions in the OMS using the approved reason code. General “carrier delay” is
not sufficient where a more specific code is available.
6.2 Lost, damaged, or materially delayed parcels
A parcel may be treated as potentially lost when:
  There is no carrier movement for five calendar days after the expected delivery date; or
  The carrier confirms loss; or
  The parcel exceeds the carrier’s investigation threshold.
Customer Care opens a claim in the Carrier Claims Portal and records the case number in the CRM. For damaged

Customer Care opens a claim in the Carrier Claims Portal and records the case number in the CRM. For damaged
goods, photographs, packaging evidence, and product value must be requested where appropriate.
Standard resolution targets are:
  Initial customer response: within one working day.
  Carrier claim submission: within two working days of confirmed exception.
  Replacement or refund decision: within three working days after required evidence is received.
Any goodwill credit above €25 requires Customer Care Team Lead approval. Credits above €100, repeated
compensation, or claims involving regulated products require approval from the Customer Care Manager.
6.3 Performance targets
Delivery Operations reports the following monthly measures by country, carrier, fulfilment site, and service type:
  On-time delivery rate: at least 95%.
  On-time dispatch rate: at least 97%.
  First-attempt delivery success: at least 92%.
  Parcel loss rate: below 0.30%.

  On-time dispatch rate: at least 97%.
  First-attempt delivery success: at least 92%.
  Parcel loss rate: below 0.30%.
  Customer contacts caused by delivery failure: monitored monthly and reviewed for trend.
A carrier below target for two consecutive months requires a corrective action plan. A third consecutive failure triggers
a commercial review and may result in volume reduction or temporary suspension.

7. Roles and Responsibilities

reviews.
  Regional Delivery Managers: Maintain country-level promises, carrier capacity rules, and exception
playbooks.
  Fulfilment Centre Managers: Meet dispatch targets, maintain scan compliance, and investigate packing
failures.
  Carrier Management: Owns contracts, scorecards, claims escalation, and corrective action plans.

  Product and Engineering: Maintain the OMS, WMS integrations, Delivery Promise Engine, and Notification
Service.
  Finance: Validates carrier credits, customer compensation reporting, and claims recovery.

1. Purpose and Overview
This procedure defines how IronStore receives, assesses, refunds, replaces, repairs, and disposes of returned
products. It covers customer-initiated returns, carrier exceptions, failed deliveries, warehouse errors, and products
rejected during quality control.
The objective is to provide a consistent customer experience while controlling reverse-logistics cost, protecting resale
value, and ensuring compliance with applicable European consumer, product-safety, environmental, and
data-protection requirements.
All returns must be traceable from the original order through final disposition. The official record is maintained in
ReturnFlow, integrated with ShopCore, WMS Atlas, carrier portals, and the finance platform LedgerOne.
2. Scope
This procedure applies to:

ReturnFlow, integrated with ShopCore, WMS Atlas, carrier portals, and the finance platform LedgerOne.
2. Scope
This procedure applies to:
  Customer returns from EU and EEA delivery destinations.
  Products fulfilled from IronStore warehouses in Germany, Poland, and the Netherlands.
  Items returned through parcel carriers, pickup services, partner drop-off points, or warehouse collections.
  Refunds, exchanges, replacements, repairs, partial refunds, and store-credit decisions.
  Products classified as resaleable, open-box, damaged, defective, unsafe, incomplete, or unsellable.
This procedure does not replace:
  The Product Safety Incident Procedure (QMS-PS-002).
  The Personal Data Handling Standard (SEC-DATA-006).
  Marketplace-specific return rules where those rules are contractually stricter.
  Supplier warranty or manufacturer repair procedures.
3. Policy Statement
IronStore accepts eligible consumer returns in line with statutory withdrawal rights and the applicable

3. Policy Statement
IronStore accepts eligible consumer returns in line with statutory withdrawal rights and the applicable
product-category terms shown at checkout. Customers must receive clear return instructions and must not be

charged an unauthorized return fee.
Returns must be processed fairly and consistently. A returned item may only be rejected, downgraded, destroyed, or
sent to a supplier when the decision is supported by documented evidence in ReturnFlow.
The standard operational targets are:
  Return request acknowledged within one business day.
  Return label or drop-off instructions issued within one business day of approval.
  Warehouse receipt scan completed within 24 hours of physical receipt.
  Initial inspection completed within two business days of receipt.
  Refund released within one business day after approval.
  Customer cases older than seven calendar days without a decision escalated to the Returns Team Lead.
4. Procedure
4.1 Return Request and Eligibility
Customer Service creates or validates the return case in ReturnFlow. The case must include:
  Order number, customer ID, SKU, quantity, and reason code.
  Purchase channel and delivery country.

  Order number, customer ID, SKU, quantity, and reason code.
  Purchase channel and delivery country.
  Photos or supporting evidence where damage, defect, or incorrect item is reported.
  Requested resolution: refund, replacement, exchange, repair, or credit.
The system checks:
  Whether the item belongs to the order.
  Whether the request is within the applicable return period.
  Whether the category has special restrictions.
  Whether a previous refund, replacement, or claim exists.
  Whether the item is subject to a safety, hygiene, or regulatory block.
Examples of restricted products include opened cosmetics, personal-care items with a broken hygiene seal, software
with an activated license, customized goods, and products legally restricted from resale after use. Customer Service
must not promise an exception without approval from the Returns Team Lead.
For approved returns, ReturnFlow generates a return authorization number (RMA) and the appropriate carrier label.

For approved returns, ReturnFlow generates a return authorization number (RMA) and the appropriate carrier label.
The RMA is valid for 14 calendar days unless a different period is shown in the case.
4.2 Return Routing and Carrier Handover
Return routing is determined by product dimensions, value, hazard classification, and warehouse capacity.
  Standard parcels use the contracted DHL Parcel Return or DPD Return service.

  Oversized items use Rhenus Home Logistics or the original delivery partner.
  Lithium-battery products must follow the Dangerous Goods Matrix DEL-DG-011.
  High-value items above €500 require tracked service and an RMA-linked label.
  Items above €1,000 require signature at handover and enhanced receipt verification.
Customers must not return products to a warehouse address manually provided by an employee. The label
generated in ReturnFlow ensures correct routing and cost allocation.
When a carrier reports a failed collection, the case is rescheduled once automatically. A second failure is assigned to
Customer Service for customer contact and alternative routing.
4.3 Warehouse Receipt
The receiving operative scans the parcel barcode and RMA into WMS Atlas. If the label is unreadable, the operative
searches by order number or carrier tracking number and creates an exception record.
At receipt, the operative must:
1. Photograph visibly damaged outer packaging.

At receipt, the operative must:
1. Photograph visibly damaged outer packaging.
2. Record parcel weight where the item is high-value, incomplete, or disputed.
3. Confirm the SKU and quantity.
4. Place the item in the correct inspection lane.
5. Update ReturnFlow with receipt date, warehouse, and condition of packaging.
Unidentified parcels are placed in the Returns Reconciliation Cage. The Returns Control Specialist investigates
within three business days using carrier data, order records, and customer contact details available in the system.
Unresolved parcels are escalated to the Logistics Operations Manager after ten business days.
4.4 Inspection and Condition Grading
The inspection associate follows the applicable category checklist in WMS Atlas. The inspection must verify:
  Product identity and serial number, where applicable.
  Functional operation using the approved test.
  Completeness of accessories, manuals, cables, and packaging.

  Functional operation using the approved test.
  Completeness of accessories, manuals, cables, and packaging.
  Signs of use, damage, contamination, or tampering.
  Safety concerns, recalled-batch indicators, and counterfeit risk.
  Customer-reported fault compared with observed condition.
The associate records findings and photographs for:
  Electronics and appliances above €250.
  Any item marked damaged, defective, incomplete, or counterfeit suspected.
  Any customer dispute involving condition or missing parts.

Condition grades are:
  A – New/resalable: Unused or indistinguishable from new, complete, and correctly packaged.
  B – Open-box: Functional, minor packaging impact, no material product damage.
  C – Used or cosmetically marked: Functional but not suitable for standard new inventory.
  D – Defective or incomplete: Requires repair, parts replacement, supplier review, or controlled liquidation.
  E – Unsafe or prohibited: Must be quarantined and prevented from resale.
Grade A items are returned to available stock only after the inventory controller confirms the SKU and quantity. Grade
B and C items are transferred to the approved outlet or refurbishment inventory pools. Grade D items are routed
according to the disposition decision. Grade E items remain in the locked quarantine area.
4.5 Resolution and Refund
The inspection result triggers a recommended resolution in ReturnFlow. The following approval limits apply:

4.5 Resolution and Refund
The inspection result triggers a recommended resolution in ReturnFlow. The following approval limits apply:
  Up to €250: Returns Team Lead may approve refund, replacement, or partial refund.
  €250–€1,000: Returns Team Lead approval plus Finance Operations review for non-standard outcomes.
  Above €1,000: Deliveries Manager and Finance Operations approval.
  Any safety, fraud, counterfeit, or legal issue: mandatory Compliance referral.
Refunds are normally issued to the original payment method through LedgerOne. Refund amount includes the
eligible product price and standard outbound delivery charge where required by the applicable withdrawal rules.
Additional delivery upgrades are not automatically refundable.
A refund may be reduced only when permitted by law and supported by evidence of customer-caused diminished
value. The decision and evidence must be recorded before the refund is released.

value. The decision and evidence must be recorded before the refund is released.
Replacement orders must be created from the original case, not as an unrelated manual order. The replacement
SKU, warehouse, expected dispatch date, and any price difference must be recorded.
4.6 Exceptions, Fraud, and Disputes
Potential fraud indicators include repeated high-value returns, serial-number mismatch, empty parcels, altered labels,
or materially different goods returned. Employees must not accuse the customer or delay a statutory refund without
authorization.
The Returns Team Lead places the case in Review Required status and refers it to Customer Protection Operations.
The review target is five business days. Confirmed abuse may result in account restrictions under the Customer
Account Controls Standard, subject to Compliance review.
Customer disputes about inspection outcomes are reviewed using warehouse photographs, scan history, carrier data,

Customer disputes about inspection outcomes are reviewed using warehouse photographs, scan history, carrier data,
and previous case notes. A written decision is issued within five business days of receiving the dispute.
4.7 Final Disposition and Environmental Controls

Disposition must be completed within 15 calendar days of warehouse receipt unless a supplier or safety
investigation is open.
Approved options are:
  Return to sellable stock.
  Transfer to outlet or refurbished inventory.
  Repair through an approved service partner.
  Return to supplier under an authorized RMA.
  Liquidation through an approved channel.
  Recycling or controlled destruction.
Employees must not place returned electronics, batteries, chemicals, textiles, or personal-care products in general
waste. WEEE, batteries, packaging, and other regulated materials must be handled through approved waste
contractors and recorded in the Environmental Compliance Register.
Products suspected to be unsafe are quarantined immediately. The Quality & Compliance Manager determines
whether a wider stock hold, supplier notification, customer notification, or regulatory report is required.

1. Purpose and Overview
This manual defines the minimum operating standards for receiving, storing, picking, packing, and dispatching
IronStore customer orders. It is intended to support safe, accurate, and traceable warehouse operations across all
product categories, including electronics, home essentials, clothing, outdoor equipment, beauty products, and other
consumer goods.
The procedures apply alongside local legal requirements, site instructions, carrier rules, and product-specific controls.
Where a local requirement is stricter than this manual, the stricter requirement applies. Deviations must be recorded
in the Atlas Warehouse Management System (WMS) and approved by the relevant Operations Manager.
2. Scope
This manual covers:
  Supplier and inter-site inbound deliveries.

2. Scope
This manual covers:
  Supplier and inter-site inbound deliveries.
  Goods receiving, inspection, labelling, and putaway.
  Inventory control, cycle counting, and location management.
  Customer order picking, packing, and dispatch.
  Returns, damaged stock, shortages, and delivery exceptions.
  Warehouse safety, security, and operational reporting.
It does not replace:
  Dangerous goods procedures under HSE-PRO-014.
  Transport planning and carrier procurement rules under DEL-TMS-002.
  Product compliance, recall, or restricted-goods procedures.
  Site-specific emergency plans and risk assessments.
3. Policy Statement
IronStore warehouses must process stock and orders accurately, safely, and within the service levels agreed with the
Deliveries function. Every stock movement must be recorded electronically, and every dispatch must be traceable to
an order, parcel, carrier, and operator or system event.

The following principles apply:
  Do not move unscanned stock except during an approved emergency process.
  Do not ship an order with an unresolved quantity, address, or product exception.
  Keep customer data visible only to staff who require it for their role.
  Use the approved packaging format for each product class.
  Escalate safety, compliance, and security concerns immediately.
4. Operating Procedures
4.1 Inbound Delivery Planning
Inbound appointments are created in Mercury TMS at least 24 hours before the planned arrival, except for approved
urgent deliveries. The booking must include:
  Supplier or origin site.
  Purchase order or transfer order number.
  Pallet, carton, and expected unit quantities.
  Product type and any handling restrictions.
  Carrier, vehicle registration, and estimated arrival time.
The Inbound Team checks the appointment against the purchase order before unloading. Unscheduled vehicles may

The Inbound Team checks the appointment against the purchase order before unloading. Unscheduled vehicles may
be held in the designated waiting area and must not unload without approval from the Inbound Supervisor.
The gatehouse or receiving desk records arrival and departure times. Drivers must follow site traffic controls, wear
required personal protective equipment (PPE), and remain in the designated area unless escorted.
4.2 Unloading and Receiving
Before unloading, the receiving operator checks:
  Vehicle condition and signs of water, pest, or security damage.
  Seal number, where applicable.
  Pallet stability and visible carton damage.
  Quantity of handling units against the delivery note.
Goods are unloaded only at the assigned bay. A second operator verifies the count for deliveries exceeding 20 pallets
or 500 units.

Shortages, overages, substitutions, and unlisted SKUs are placed in the Inbound Hold location. The Inbound

4.3 Inspection and Product Controls
A sample inspection is performed on each inbound delivery. The standard sample is:
  Five cartons for deliveries of up to 100 cartons.
  Ten cartons for deliveries over 100 cartons.
  The full delivery where damage or repeated quality issues are identified.
Operators check packaging, labels, product identity, accessories, and visible defects. Electronics with serial numbers
must be scanned individually. Beauty products, food-contact items, and other dated goods must meet the minimum
remaining shelf-life specified in the purchase order.
Damaged or suspect stock is labelled QUARANTINE – DO NOT SHIP, moved to the secure quarantine area, and
photographed in Atlas WMS. The Quality Lead decides whether stock is released, reworked, returned, or scrapped.
Staff must not repair, repackage, or relabel goods without documented approval.
4.4 Putaway and Storage

Staff must not repair, repackage, or relabel goods without documented approval.
4.4 Putaway and Storage
Atlas WMS generates the putaway task based on product dimensions, turnover, handling restrictions, and location
capacity. Operators must scan both the product and destination location before placing stock.
Storage rules include:
  Heavy items below shoulder height.
  Fragile items in protected shelving or designated cages.
  High-value electronics in access-controlled locations.
  Aerosols, liquids, batteries, and other controlled products in approved areas.
  Clothing and textiles kept dry and protected from contamination.
  Expiry-controlled stock managed using FEFO: first expiry, first out.
A location must not exceed its weight, volume, or pallet-height limit. Empty locations are kept clear, labelled, and
available in Atlas WMS. Any unlabelled or inaccessible location is reported to the Inventory Controller.

4.5 Inventory Accuracy
All stock adjustments require a reason code and electronic approval. The following approval levels apply:
  Up to €50 cost value: Inventory Controller.
  €50.01–€500: Warehouse Operations Manager.
  Above €500, repeated variance, or suspected theft: Head of Deliveries and Loss Prevention.
Cycle counts are completed daily according to the Atlas WMS count queue. A location is recounted when the first
count differs from the system by more than:

  One unit for serialized products.
  Two units or 2%, whichever is greater, for standard products.
  One case for case-managed inventory.
The counter must not edit the expected quantity before completing the recount. Variances are investigated using
receiving records, pick scans, replenishment tasks, and dispatch confirmations.
4.6 Picking
Customer orders are released to the warehouse through Atlas WMS according to the cut-off schedule published by
Planning. The default same-day release cut-off is 14:00 local time, although site-specific cut-offs may differ.
Picking operators must:
1. Scan the task, location, and product.
2. Confirm quantity and, where required, serial number or batch.
3. Place items in the assigned tote or container.
4. Report empty, damaged, or incorrect stock immediately.
5. Close the task only after the physical movement is complete.
Operators must not pick from a location showing a quarantine, blocked, or investigation status. Substitutions are

Operators must not pick from a location showing a quarantine, blocked, or investigation status. Substitutions are
prohibited unless approved by Customer Care and enabled in the order system.
For multi-item orders, totes must remain separated by order or wave. Totes left unattended for more than 30 minutes
must be returned to the designated staging area.
4.7 Packing and Quality Check
Packing stations must use the packaging recommendation displayed in Atlas WMS. The packer confirms:
  Correct order and recipient details.
  Product quantity and condition.
  Required accessories, documents, and promotional inserts.
  Carrier service and destination country.
  Packaging suitability and closure.
A second check is required for high-value orders, orders containing more than five SKUs, and any order flagged by
the fraud or Customer Care systems. The checker records the verification in Atlas WMS.

Packages must be sealed securely, with no loose labels or exposed product. Customer information must not be
visible through transparent packaging. Batteries, liquids, aerosols, and fragile goods require the approved inner
protection and external markings.
The packer prints the carrier label only after the parcel weight is recorded. A weight variance above 10% from the
system expectation triggers a recheck before dispatch.

4.8 Dispatch and Handover
Completed parcels are scanned into the correct carrier cage or dispatch lane. Carrier manifests are generated in
Mercury TMS and reconciled against the physical parcel count before loading.
The Dispatch Supervisor verifies:
  Parcel count by carrier and service.
  Manifest totals and exception parcels.
  Cage or vehicle seal number.
  Collection time and driver identity.
No parcel may be handed to a carrier without a successful dispatch scan. Missed collections, rejected parcels, or
manifest differences are logged in the Delivery Incident Register within one hour.
Standard dispatch targets are:
  98.5% of parcels scanned before the carrier collection cut-off.
  99.7% order-pick accuracy.
  99.5% parcel-to-manifest reconciliation.
  Same-day escalation for any lost or untraceable parcel.
4.9 Returns and Delivery Exceptions
Customer returns are received against a return authorisation or carrier return reference. The Returns Team classifies
each item as:

Customer returns are received against a return authorisation or carrier return reference. The Returns Team classifies
each item as:
  Resalable.
  Open-box or rework required.
  Damaged.
  Incomplete.
  Suspected counterfeit or compliance concern.
The classification, photographs, and disposition are recorded in Atlas WMS within two working days. Refund
decisions remain with Customer Care and Finance.
Delivery exceptions, including wrong item, missing parcel, damage in transit, or address failure, are recorded against
the original order. The Deliveries Support Desk owns carrier enquiries and must issue the first status update within
one working day.
Suspected theft, deliberate damage, or repeated carrier loss is escalated to Loss Prevention and the Head of
Deliveries.
5. Safety, Security, and Housekeeping

All warehouse staff must complete site induction and role-specific training before working independently. Required
PPE is displayed at each site entrance and work area.
Mandatory rules:
  Do not walk beneath raised forks or suspended loads.
  Keep pedestrian routes and fire exits clear.
  Use mechanical aids for loads above the site manual-handling limit of 15 kg.
  Report spills, damaged racking, blocked exits, and unsafe equipment immediately.
  Do not use phones while operating warehouse equipment.
  Challenge or report unidentified persons in restricted areas.
Forklift and powered-equipment operators must hold current site-approved certification. Equipment defects are
tagged OUT OF SERVICE and reported through the SafeTrack incident system.
At shift end, operators clear waste, return scanners to charging points, secure high-value stock, and leave
workstations ready for the next shift.

7. Performance Reporting and Escalation
The Operations Manager reviews the daily dashboard in Pulse BI. Minimum measures include:
  Inbound receipt completion.
  Inventory accuracy and unresolved variances.
  Pick and pack accuracy.
  Orders released before cut-off.
  Parcel dispatch and manifest reconciliation.
  Damage, return, and carrier exception rates.
  Safety incidents and near misses.

Any red KPI for two consecutive working days requires a corrective action plan. A serious safety incident, regulatory
concern, suspected fraud, or material customer-data exposure must be escalated immediately to the Head of
Deliveries and the relevant Compliance contact.
